records.name: Antibody-drug conjugate (ADC)
records.tldr: An antibody-drug conjugate links a target-binding antibody to an active drug. Binding, delivery, release and drug action each matter, and normal tissues can also be exposed.
records.summary: The antibody recognizes an accessible antigen; the attachment chemistry and linker affect stability and release; the payload acts through its own molecular mechanism. Cytotoxic examples include TOP1 inhibitors, tubulin inhibitors and DNA-damaging agents. Uptake and lysosomal processing are important for many constructs, while some linkers also release drug outside cells. A surface antigen can be a delivery address without being a driver the tumor depends on. The dose, mean loading, loading distribution, released species and exposure must be interpreted for the finished product. There is no universal fold improvement in the therapeutic window.

records.name: Site-specific conjugation & linker chemistry
records.tldr: Attachment sites, loading and linker chemistry shape the finished conjugate. More controlled manufacture can help, but safety and effectiveness require evidence for that product.
records.summary: Conventional attachment to available lysines or reduced cysteines can produce mixtures of attachment sites and loading states. Engineered sites and other selective chemistries aim to control these features. In one engineered-cysteine study, a near-homogeneous anti-MUC16 conjugate retained mouse antitumor activity and was tolerated at higher doses in rats and monkeys than its conventional comparator. That result supports a design strategy, not a guarantee of identical loading or improved human outcomes for every site-specific product. Hydrophilic drug-linker designs have also reduced accelerated clearance in studied high-loading constructs.

records.principle: Attachment site, site occupancy, linker chemistry and released chemical species are separate properties of the complete conjugate.
strengths: More control of attachment and loading in suitable designs
Can support defined single- or multiple-payload constructs
limitations: Loading distribution and impurities still require measurement
Stability, aggregation, exposure and safety remain product-specific

records.name: Linker (ADC)
records.tldr: The linker connects antibody and payload. Its chemistry affects where the drug separates and which active chemical species becomes available.
records.summary: Cleavable linkers can respond to enzymes, reduction or hydrolysis under specified conditions. Release is construct-specific and need not occur exclusively inside a cancer cell. A noncleavable linker can remain on the payload while the antibody is broken down, leaving an active amino-acid-linker-payload catabolite. For T-DM1, Lys-SMCC-DM1 must leave the lysosome to reach its intracellular site of action; SLC46A3 directly transports this catabolite in experimental systems. The released species can differ from the unconjugated parent drug in transport and permeability.

records.name: Drug-to-antibody ratio (DAR)
records.tldr: DAR usually reports the average number of payload molecules attached per antibody. The average can hide a mixture of differently loaded molecules.
records.summary: Drug-to-antibody ratio describes payload loading. A preparation can contain antibodies with different numbers and sites of attachment, so the reported mean does not specify every molecule. Two preparations with the same mean can differ in their loading distribution and attachment chemistry. Higher loading can increase cell-assay potency while also changing hydrophobicity, aggregation, clearance and tolerated exposure. Hamblett and colleagues separated differently loaded versions of one anti-CD30 conjugate and found that greater cell-assay potency did not translate into a proportional mouse treatment advantage. That experiment does not set one optimal DAR for every product.

notes: Site-directed attachment can improve control, but occupancy, remaining heterogeneity, stability and function still need measurement. Hydrophobic-interaction chromatography and suitable mass-spectrometric methods can characterize loading; an average alone cannot establish product equivalence or clinical benefit. For multiple payload types, retain each component’s loading instead of inventing its share from total DAR.

records.name: Bystander effect (ADC)
records.tldr: A conjugate can harm neighboring cells when an active released species reaches them, including neighbors with little or none of the delivery target.
records.summary: Bystander killing is a local drug effect, distinct from radiation crossfire or immune memory. It depends on the chemical species actually released, its transport through membranes and tissue, the concentration reaching neighboring cells and their susceptibility. Ogitani and colleagues compared a permeable DXd species, a poorly permeable alternative and the T-DM1 catabolite Lys-SMCC-DM1. Their coculture and mixed-tumor mouse experiments showed neighboring target-negative-cell killing with the permeable DXd construct; a separate target-negative tumor on the opposite flank did not respond in that experiment. These findings support a local mechanism in those models, not a universal safety or patient-benefit claim.

notes: Neither a cleavable-linker label nor a permeability result alone proves bystander killing in a tumor. More chemical spread can also expose normal cells, so it is not an efficacy ranking.

records.name: Cross-resistance
records.tldr: Resistance to one treatment can also reduce sensitivity to another when the treatments share a vulnerable step. A different drug name does not establish an independent mechanism.
records.summary: For antibody-drug conjugates, resistance can involve antigen access or uptake, intracellular processing and transport, the payload’s molecular target, drug efflux, or the cell’s response to injury. Breast cancer models selected for resistance to T-DXd or sacituzumab govitecan showed shared payload-associated resistance and renewed activity with some non-TOP1 conjugates. A selected patient cohort and functional experiments also linked particular TOP1 mutations to reduced sensitivity to SN-38 and deruxtecan. These are distinct forms of evidence, not proof that every resistant tumor has the same cause or that switching class improves outcomes for everyone.

notes: Changing the antibody target can leave shared efflux or cell-response resistance intact. Changing payload mechanism can leave a delivery or processing defect intact. A transporter may handle more than one drug, and different tumor cells can carry different resistance mechanisms. Collateral sensitivity is the separate possibility that adaptation to one treatment increases sensitivity to another.

records.name: ADC sequencing
records.tldr: ADC sequencing asks whether a second conjugate can help after the first fails, especially when it carries the same payload class. The earlier response and reason for stopping matter.
records.summary: A second conjugate may retain activity after a first, but neither shared nor different target names settle the outcome. Payload cross-resistance, altered delivery and tumor evolution can all matter. Retrospective treatment sequences are affected by who lived long enough and remained fit to receive another drug, treatment line, prior response and clinician selection. A selected cohort with post-treatment plasma profiling and laboratory TOP1-mutant experiments supports a resistance hypothesis; cell and mouse payload-switching experiments test a different question. Neither design establishes the best clinical sequence.

notes: Mechanism experiments can compare an intact conjugate with its free payload, measure uptake and released species, and perturb a suspected transporter or resistance gene. These experiments require controls and do not by themselves validate a clinical test for choosing the next ADC. A trial in ADC-naive patients cannot establish effectiveness specifically after progression on a prior TOP1 ADC.

records.name: Bispecific ADC
records.tldr: A bispecific antibody-drug conjugate uses two recognition features to deliver a payload. Its design can change delivery; phase 3 testing still evaluates the complete drug.
records.summary: Different-antigen designs recognize two proteins; biparatopic designs recognize distinct epitopes on one protein. Depending on the molecule and cell, the design may favor binding to either target, combined binding, receptor clustering or transport through an internalizing partner. A biparatopic HER2 conjugate carrying a tubulysin derivative promoted clustering and lysosomal trafficking in preclinical models. A separate HER2-by-prolactin-receptor study increased uptake and cell killing by linking a slower-trafficking target to a rapidly internalized partner. These experiments do not isolate a universal clinical advantage of two-target binding. Clinical examples need their own evidence: the registry identifies izalontamab brengitecan (EGFR-by-HER3) in the phase 3 BL-B01D1-307/PANKU-Breast02 study of previously treated advanced triple-negative breast cancer against chemotherapy. That design does not isolate the added contribution of the bispecific format over another ADC.

strengths: Can alter recognition or intracellular delivery in suitable designs
Offers a way to test heterogeneous target expression

Two binding specificities do not establish two payload mechanisms
Selectivity, loading, release and toxicity require construct-specific evidence

records.name: Monoclonal antibodies
records.tldr: A monoclonal antibody is a manufactured protein with a defined recognition design. Its other functional parts and the target biology determine what follows binding.
records.summary: Monoclonal does not by itself mean patient-specific or physically identical molecules in every detail. A therapeutic preparation can contain characterized molecular variants, including different sugar modifications. Recognition can be used to block an interaction, recruit immune effectors, carry a drug or radionuclide, or bridge cells, depending on the complete product. A shared target name does not establish the same epitope or action. Binding, functional activity, exposure and clinical benefit answer different questions.

Lymphoma: internalization is not an immutable property of the antigen name. Lim and colleagues found that target-cell Fc-gamma receptor IIb promoted internalization of rituximab-CD20 complexes, with substantial variation across the studied B-cell malignancies. This changes antibody exposure and access for effector cells; it does not establish that any particular CD20 conjugate will deliver an effective or safe payload.
records.principle: A defined recognition region makes contact; the assembled product and biological setting determine the tested effect.
strengths: Defined molecular recognition can support different therapeutic mechanisms
limitations: Healthy tissue can share the recognized target
Human or humanized sequence does not establish freedom from adverse effects
Identity or binding alone does not establish potency or clinical benefit

records.name: Radioligand therapy (beta emitters)
records.tldr: A target-binding molecule carries a radionuclide whose emissions deposit radiation in tissue. Distribution and retention help determine tumor and normal-organ exposure.
records.summary: Lutetium-177 therapies deliver beta-particle radiation through target-binding molecules. VISION tested PSMA-targeted treatment added to protocol-permitted standard care in selected, previously treated metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. NETTER-1 tested lutetium-177-dotatate in progressive, somatostatin-receptor-positive midgut neuroendocrine tumors. Their clinical results belong to those populations and products, rather than every tumor expressing the target. Small molecules, peptides and antibodies have different distribution and clearance even when directed at a shared target.

notes: Radioactive activity is a decay rate in becquerels; absorbed dose is deposited energy per mass in gray. A single bright image is not time-integrated exposure. Dosimetry combines suitable activity measurements or models over time with tissue geometry and emission properties. Neither the targeting-molecule mass nor the administered activity alone specifies tumor dose.

Radioimmunotherapy uses an antibody carrier. The broader radiopharmaceutical category also includes organ-seeking products without a separate targeting ligand. Not every attachment uses a metal chelator. Alpha and beta emissions have different path and energy-deposition properties; neither label alone ranks safety or effectiveness. Daughter redistribution and microscopic geometry can matter.
records.principle: Where the complete radioactive product travels, how long it remains and which emissions reach tissue jointly determine radiation delivery.
strengths: Targeted delivery of radiation through an accessible molecular feature
Emitted particles can reach neighboring cells
limitations: Kidney, marrow and other normal-tissue exposure can limit treatment
A positive scan alone does not establish absorbed dose or clinical benefit
Results from one radionuclide or carrier do not establish equivalence of another

records.name: Dosimetry
records.tldr: Dosimetry estimates the radiation energy deposited per unit mass in a specified tissue or target. The estimate depends on measurements, geometry and a stated model.
records.summary: Absorbed dose is reported in gray, equivalent to joules per kilogram. It differs from radioactive activity in becquerels, which describes decays per second. For a radiopharmaceutical, dose estimation uses the location and time course of radioactivity, the emissions and the target’s mass and geometry. Suitable calibrated serial imaging can inform the estimate; it does not turn one uptake value into a measured tumor dose. External-beam and internal-emitter methods answer related dose questions using different inputs.

links.label: EPA: activity, absorbed dose and their units
MIRD pamphlet 22: alpha-particle radiobiology and dosimetry (2010)
FDA: nonclinical development of oncology therapeutic radiopharmaceuticals (2019)

notes: Report the method, time sampling, target volume and uncertainty. An organ-average dose can hide uneven cellular exposure, especially for short-range alpha emissions. Absorbed dose and clinical outcome remain distinct; no single organ threshold or schedule applies to all products.

records.name: Radioligand dosimetry
records.tldr: Radioligand dosimetry estimates radiation deposited in tumors and normal tissues from where radioactivity goes and how it changes with time.
records.summary: Calibrated activity measurements, often from suitable serial SPECT or PET imaging, inform a time-activity model. Time-integrated decays, emission properties, tissue mass and spatial assumptions then inform absorbed dose. Equal uptake on an early scan can be followed by different retention and different doses. Administered activity is an input, not a substitute for patient- or tissue-level dosimetry. The estimates can support evaluation of dosing strategies, but improved outcomes from a particular adaptation require their own evidence.

EPA: activity, absorbed dose and their units
FDA: nonclinical development of oncology therapeutic radiopharmaceuticals (2019)

notes: Physical decay, biological clearance and radioactive daughters all affect interpretation. Alpha-emitter dosimetry may need additional microscopic considerations. FDA’s cited document addresses nonclinical development; it is not a universal clinical dosing protocol or evidence of a jurisdiction-wide reimbursement requirement.
records.principle: Estimate activity through time in specified source regions, then calculate the energy deposited in relevant target regions with explicit assumptions.
strengths: Makes tumor and normal-tissue exposure explicit
Can evaluate why the same administered activity produces different dose estimates
limitations: Calibration, time sampling and segmentation affect estimates
Organ averages can miss uneven microscopic exposure
Method-specific dose estimates do not establish a universal clinical threshold

records.name: Radio-antibody & radio-ADC
records.tldr: Radioimmunotherapy uses an antibody or antibody fragment to carry a radionuclide. Its radiation delivery and safety depend on the complete labeled product.
records.summary: An antibody provides recognition while the radionuclide provides radiation. This differs from releasing a small-molecule cytotoxic drug after intracellular processing. Attachment chemistry depends on the isotope and product; a chelator is not required for every radionuclide. In a historical phase 2 study, lutetium-177-J591 targeted PSMA in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer and produced substantial hematologic toxicity. That disease-specific experience does not establish current approval, breast-cancer efficacy or the suitability of every ADC antigen for radioimmunotherapy.

records.principle: The labeled antibody’s distribution and retention, radionuclide emissions and tissue geometry determine where radiation is deposited.
strengths: Can deliver radiation with an antibody recognition route

records.name: ADC analytes and exposure
records.tldr: An antibody-drug conjugate and its released drug do not follow one shared concentration curve. The measured chemical form matters.
records.summary: A conjugate assay measures antibody carrying payload, or antibody-bound drug, according to the validated method. Total antibody includes conjugated and unconjugated antibody; unconjugated payload measures released drug separately. Active metabolites or catabolites can add further relevant species. Concentration, time course and exposure therefore belong to a named analyte. A conjugate dose in milligrams per kilogram is not the same quantity as the mass of free payload reaching a tumor or the blood.

For a construct carrying different payloads, keep each chemical identity, loading distribution, release behavior and exposure distinct. A manufactured loading ratio does not establish the ratio reaching tissue over time. The same total DAR does not establish equal loading of each component or equal biological activity.

records.name: CHK1 inhibitor payloads
records.tldr: A CHK1-inhibitor conjugate carries a drug that interferes with a replication-stress checkpoint. A published conference abstract reports a HER2-directed preclinical example.
records.summary: CHK1 inhibition is the cargo mechanism only when the inhibitor is physically attached to the conjugate. The AACR 2026 abstract describes engineered-cysteine trastuzumab, a cleavable linker and a CHK1-inhibitor payload. The investigators tested cells and a HER2-positive breast-cancer xenograft model. This establishes a publicly described payload design and model experiment, separate from giving an oral checkpoint inhibitor alongside another ADC. It does not establish human safety, benefit after a TOP1 ADC or a treatment-selection rule.

notes: The antibody delivery antigen and the payload’s checkpoint target answer different questions. The proposed advantage depends on sufficient intracellular release and checkpoint dependence, not a HER2 or replication-stress label alone. The conference abstract reports limited model safety observations; lack of mouse weight loss cannot establish human marrow safety or a clinical therapeutic window.

An earlier 2020 study attached the checkpoint inhibitor AZD7762 to an antibody. The conjugate recognized the tested cell-surface target but lacked efficacy in that delivery experiment; the investigators pursued protease-activated cell-penetrating peptides instead. Physical attachment and target binding therefore did not establish a useful intracellular effect. This negative result does not establish that every CHK1-directed conjugate must fail.

The 2026 A067 conference abstract screened exatecan with prexasertib in cancer-cell and blood-progenitor assays. It proposes a candidate pair for dual-payload development; the abstract does not itself document both chemicals attached to a tested antibody. Pairwise synergy, a constructed dual-cargo product and a patient therapeutic window are separate claims.

NCT02124148 lists prexasertib and cetuximab as separately administered drugs with different schedules. It is not evidence of a cetuximab conjugate carrying a CHK1 inhibitor. Registry design, observed pharmacodynamic changes and patient outcomes also require separate interpretation.

records.name: PARP inhibitor payloads
records.tldr: A PARP-inhibitor payload attaches a repair-targeting drug to an antibody. A published preclinical abstract describes a TROP2 conjugate carrying a PARP1-selective inhibitor.
records.summary: The AACR 2025 abstract describes a TROP2 antibody joined through a cleavable linker to a PARP1-selective inhibitor. Cell comparisons included the conjugate, free payload and antibody alone; a breast-cancer xenograft experiment compared their activity and blood-cell effects. The reported activity varied between tested cell models, illustrating that more delivery antigen is not sufficient to establish payload sensitivity. This is a conference-abstract proof of concept, not clinical evidence that antibody delivery reverses PARP resistance or removes systemic toxicity.

notes: An approved PARP-inhibitor pill, a free PARP drug combined with an ADC and a physically attached PARP payload are different products and evidence questions. Retain the actual conjugated chemical species, linker, release and exposure. A repair-gene variant alone does not prove the tumor’s current functional dependence or establish eligibility for an experimental conjugate.

records.name: ATR and CHK1 inhibitors
records.tldr: ATR and CHK1 inhibitors interfere with checkpoint responses to stressed DNA replication. Researchers test whether particular tumors depend on those responses enough to create a treatment window.
records.summary: ATR and downstream checkpoint signaling help cells respond when replication is stressed. Repair defects or other tumor features can increase dependence in specific models, but a gene name or stress marker alone does not establish patient benefit. A phase 1 camonsertib study enrolled selected advanced solid tumors with predicted sensitizing repair-gene alterations; a separate small prexasertib pilot studied previously treated BRCA-wild-type triple-negative breast cancer. These are different drugs, populations and designs. Blood-cell toxicity remained important, and neither study validates every proposed repair-defect biomarker.

Appropriate target, repair-state and exposure controls help distinguish delivery, inhibitor activity and cell susceptibility. Changing from a TOP1 payload does not guarantee bypass of a shared delivery or resistance defect.

strengths: Tests a repair- or replication-stress dependence hypothesis
Can be studied with DNA-damaging treatments using appropriate safety controls
limitations: Blood-cell toxicity can limit exposure
Biomarker and combination results belong to the tested drug, population and regimen

records.name: Histone lactylation
records.tldr: Lactate can contribute to a chemical modification of histone proteins. Experiments connect this mark to gene regulation in particular cell states and disease models.
records.summary: Lactylation adds a lactate-derived modification to histone lysine residues, rather than changing the DNA sequence. The original study identified this mark in human and mouse cells and investigated its timing and gene-regulatory effects in stimulated macrophages. A later mechanistic study in EGFR T790M-positive tumor models connected radiation, LDHA-dependent lactate production, histone lactylation and DNA-repair responses. Its cell, organoid and xenograft experiments provide a context-specific mechanism hypothesis, not a validated clinical radiation-selection test.

notes: Bulk lactate concentration, a particular histone modification, its genomic location, RNA output and DNA-repair activity are different measurements. The radiation study combined biochemical and chromatin measurements with genetic or pharmacological perturbations. A high lactate value alone does not establish that this mechanism is present, dominant or targetable in another tumor.

records.name: CAR-T cell therapy
records.tldr: CAR-T therapy uses T cells carrying an engineered receptor. Approved products treat selected blood cancers, with product-specific eligibility and safety requirements.
records.summary:
CAR-T cell therapy uses T cells carrying a chimeric antigen receptor to recognize a target. FDA-approved products include CD19- and BCMA-directed CAR-T cells for selected blood cancers, including B-cell leukemias, lymphomas and multiple myeloma. The individual product label defines the treatment setting and eligibility. A common autologous approach collects a person’s T cells, engineers and expands them outside the body, then infuses them back; conditioning and follow-up depend on the protocol.

A common antibody-derived CAR joins an external binding region, a hinge or spacer, a membrane anchor and intracellular signaling domains. The receptor is a protein; its encoding instructions and the living cell carrying it are different objects. Approved products and experimental constructs differ in cell source, receptor, manufacturing and clinical setting. Product labels and trial records define their actual uses; a platform name does not establish eligibility or benefit.

In early work, Gross, Waks and Eshhar joined antibody-variable regions to T-cell receptor components in 1989. Eshhar and colleagues subsequently tested single-chain antibody-binding regions joined to gamma or zeta signaling chains in 1993. These experimental designs helped separate recognition from the signaling machinery attached to it.

FDA-approved examples include tisagenlecleucel, axicabtagene ciloleucel, lisocabtagene maraleucel, brexucabtagene autoleucel, obecabtagene autoleucel, idecabtagene vicleucel and ciltacabtagene autoleucel. Their labeled diseases, treatment settings and eligibility differ; the individual product records retain those distinctions.

The full binder, spacer, anchor, signaling arrangement and cell preparation still matter.

CD28 and 4-1BB are borrowed intracellular signaling regions, not separately administered receptors. Kawalekar compared metabolic and memory features in defined human-cell experiments. Ramos co-infused two specified second- and third-generation products in lymphoma; different expansion and persistence did not isolate comparative clinical benefit. Neither study ranks all products by signaling-domain name.

Binding, surface CAR expression, activation, proliferation and completed target-cell killing are distinct readouts. Compare otherwise matched constructs, target-positive and target-negative cells, healthy-tissue targets and unstimulated activity. Hudecek found that particular IgG-derived spacers could support killing in a dish yet impair activity in mouse models through Fc interactions.

A peptide-HLA target is an exception to blanket HLA-independent descriptions. Rafiq tested a WT1 peptide presented by HLA-A*02:01 in cell and mouse models; this was a proof of concept, not evidence that every intracellular protein or every HLA type is addressable by that construct.

A 2024 preprint used a pooled signaling-domain library, repeated stimulation and single-cell sequencing to study how domain arrangement affected T-cell states over time. Its membrane-proximal-domain findings are construct-and-assay observations, not a clinical ranking of domains or a validation of pooled-screen hits as treatments.

FDA initiated boxed-warning changes in 2024 for the risk of T-cell malignancies after the then-approved BCMA- or CD19-directed autologous CAR T-cell products. Its communication calls for lifelong monitoring for secondary malignancies. This is a scoped regulatory warning, not a claim that every type of engineered immune cell has the same risk.

In June 2025, FDA eliminated REMS requirements for the named autologous CAR T-cell products in its notice. Product warnings and safety monitoring continued. The manufacturer postmarketing observational studies with 15-year follow-up described in that notice are different from the lifelong patient-monitoring statement in the earlier safety communication.

Relapse mechanisms need separate investigation. Sotillo found CD19 sequence and splicing changes affecting recognition in B-ALL relapse material and experiments. Deng found infusion-product transcriptional features associated with outcomes in a selected cohort of 24 large B-cell lymphoma infusion products; those associations did not prove that one engineered modification would correct every failure.
records.principle: A common CAR presents a binder outside the cell and signaling domains inside it, connected through a spacer and transmembrane region. Conventional surface-antigen recognition can bypass peptide-HLA presentation; specialized peptide-HLA-targeting CARs retain the relevant HLA and antigen-processing requirements.
strengths: Antigen-directed recognition in engineered T cells
Established uses for specific products in selected blood cancers
limitations: Shared healthy-tissue targets and inflammatory, neurologic or blood-count harms
Manufacturing, access and cost depend on the product and setting
Antigen heterogeneity, cell state, tissue access and local inhibition

records.name: Armoured, logic-gated & next-gen CARs
aka: T cells redirected for universal cytokine-mediated killing
records.tldr: Armored immune cells add a specified function, such as cytokine support or a changed response to an inhibitory signal. Each added function brings its own activity and safety questions.
records.summary: Armoring adds functions beyond a basic recognition receptor. Designs include continuous, activation-induced or surface-held cytokine support and modifications to particular inhibitory responses. A dominant-negative TGF-beta receptor is a receptor variant that interferes with signaling; it is different from deleting a receptor gene. Recognition logic and cell-elimination switches are separate design choices. None guarantees access to every tumor, coverage of antigen-negative cells or protection of healthy tissue.

NFAT can also respond to physiological T-cell receptor stimulation, so activation-responsive is not automatically CAR-exclusive or tumor-exclusive. Narayan tested a PSMA CAR with a dominant-negative TGF-beta receptor in a prostate-cancer phase 1 study; a fatal event occurred with severe cytokine release syndrome and concurrent sepsis. Resistance to one signal was not resistance to every inhibitory pathway or every harm.

Use otherwise matched cells with and without the added function, with relevant suppressive signals, repeated stimulation and healthy-tissue targets. Cytokine concentration, viable-cell abundance and killing at a specified time answer different questions. Greater expansion alone does not establish a wider safety window.
records.principle: Specify the added gene or receptor, the cells carrying it, when and where it is expressed, and the response it is intended to change. Test its contribution alongside the behavior and harms of the complete product.
strengths: Experimental ways to address a specified inhibitory signal or add supportive activity
limitations: Local triggering does not establish local-only exposure
Added functions may also increase harmful activity
Component effects and whole-product clinical outcomes need separate evidence

records.name: Logic-gated therapeutics (AND, NOT gates)
records.tldr: Recognition circuits combine inputs to broaden target coverage or restrict activation. AND-like, OR-like, inhibitory and sequential designs have different failure modes and need direct testing.
records.summary: In cell-based examples, split and tuned activation/costimulation can implement an AND-like requirement, either-target recognition can broaden coverage with an OR-like rule, and a protective-antigen input can inhibit activity. SynNotch-to-CAR systems induce a second receptor over time, creating a primed state rather than requiring two antigens to remain simultaneously present on one cell. Thresholds, expression, decay and movement between tissues matter. An intended rule is a design hypothesis, not proof that healthy tissue is spared or that the complete product improves outcomes.

Coverage and selectivity can be explored as separate design goals
limitations: Stricter gates may miss tumors lacking a required input
Broader OR recognition may add healthy-tissue recognition routes

records.name: CAR-NK & CAR-macrophage
records.tldr: CAR-NK cells and CAR-macrophages add recognition receptors to different innate immune-cell families. Their native functions, starting materials and engineered support still matter.
records.summary: A CAR adds a recognition input rather than replacing the effector cell. NK cells retain activating and inhibitory receptor inputs; macrophages have different functions, including phagocytosis and antigen handling. Donor blood, cord blood, pluripotent-cell-derived products and NK cell lines are distinct starting materials. Product-specific manufacture, expansion, persistence, tissue access, compatibility and harms need their own evidence. A small favorable blood-cancer study does not rank every NK product as safer than every T-cell product or establish solid-tumor benefit.

CAR recognition, native NK activity and missing-self recognition are different inputs. An NK cell is not a natural killer T cell, and absence of a conventional TCR does not remove every compatibility, rejection or product-contamination concern.

Attribution to a native receptor needs an independent perturbation with controls for changes in other ligands and target-cell viability. Binding, cytokine or granule release, viable-cell abundance and completed killing should not be substituted for one another.

Klichinsky engineered human macrophages and studied antigen-specific phagocytosis, inflammatory changes and tumor effects in cell and mouse models. These results describe a macrophage construct and those models; they do not establish a clinical efficacy or persistence ranking against CAR-NK or CAR-T.

strengths: Different native effector functions can be investigated alongside CAR recognition
Some NK products have shown allogeneic feasibility in defined early studies
limitations: Persistence depends on source and engineered support
Host rejection, inflammatory harms and manufacturing quality remain product-specific questions
Cell and mouse results do not establish clinical benefit in solid tumors

records.name: NK cell therapy and CAR-NK
records.tldr: NK-cell therapies use natural killer cells, with or without an added CAR. Cell source and engineering determine what must be tested for persistence, compatibility, activity and harms.
records.summary: Natural killer cells integrate activating and inhibitory signals and can be prepared from different starting materials. Some products use donor or cord-blood cells; others use pluripotent-cell-derived cells or cell lines. A CAR supplies an additional recognition route, while cytokines or other engineering can alter subsequent behavior. Early clinical observations belong to the actual source, construct, conditioning and population studied. They do not establish universal compatibility, negligible inflammatory risk or uniformly poor persistence.

records.name: NK cell
records.tldr: Natural killer cells integrate activating and inhibitory inputs to respond to abnormal cells. An added CAR supplies another recognition route; missing self is one input rather than a guarantee of killing.
records.summary: Some inhibitory NK receptors recognize self HLA class I, while activating receptors respond to other features. Reduced self display can weaken an inhibitory input, but the NK cell, its prior education, activating signals and target context still determine the response. NK cells can also contribute antibody-dependent killing through Fc receptors. Donor-derived or engineered NK-cell products need their own compatibility, persistence and safety assessment rather than a blanket claim that matching or rejection never matters. The principle comes from mouse experiments: lymphoma cells selected for loss of H-2 were less malignant at low dose and were rejected by a non-adaptive mechanism, which suggested that natural killer cells are effectors in a defence system geared to detect reduced self MHC (Kärre et al., 1986); that does not guarantee the same outcome for any human tumour. MHC class I molecules are ligands for killer-cell immunoglobulin-like receptors (Parham, 2005): two-domain KIR2D receptors bind HLA-C alleles and three-domain KIR3D receptors bind HLA-A and HLA-B alleles, and the KIR family includes activating as well as inhibitory members (Mariuzza et al., 2025). CD94/NKG2A binds HLA-E, and HLA-E surface expression was enough to protect target cells from lysis by CD94/NKG2A-positive NK clones (Braud et al., 1998). NKG2D binds class I-related proteins including MICA, MICB and ULBP1 to 3 (Mariuzza et al., 2025), and engagement of NKG2D activated NK and gamma-delta T-cell cytolysis against epithelial tumour cells expressing MICA (Bauer et al., 1999). No single activating receptor dominates, since NK cells integrate synergistic signals from several (Long et al., 2013), and responsiveness depends on prior education: in human cell experiments, cytokine stimulation let hyporesponsive NK cells acquire KIR and function when the cognate MHC was present (Juelke et al., 2009). Loss of one HLA allele is not loss of all class I. Loss of beta-2 microglobulin removed surface class I in one of four relapsing melanoma patients (Zaretsky et al., 2016), and because HLA-E is assembled with beta-2 microglobulin, the KIR and NKG2A restraints would be expected to lift together; that last step is an inference not tested in the cited abstracts. A flow-based cytotoxicity assay that stains target and effector nuclei separately and distinguishes live from dead nuclei has been validated with NK-92 cells, CAR-T cells and tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes (Rabinovich et al., 2019). Target death is not a count of effector cells that released granule contents: surface CD107a marked NK cells that degranulated after stimulation with MHC-devoid targets and correlated with lysis, and also marked a large subset that did not secrete cytokine, so different readouts count different cells (Alter et al., 2004). CD16 is a low-affinity Fc receptor for IgG that mediates antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity by NK cells (Liu, 2022), a route separate from missing-self recognition. Neither assay readout shows tumour entry or clinical benefit.

records.name: In vivo CAR-T
records.tldr: An in vivo delivery product carries receptor-encoding instructions into cells inside the body. Its dose is different from the later number and activity of engineered cells.
records.summary: Targeted delivery can supply CAR-encoding instructions to cells inside the body, using formats such as a viral vector or an mRNA lipid nanoparticle. This changes where engineering happens; it does not mean the active cells are donor-derived. Delivery targeting, cancer-antigen recognition, generated-cell abundance, receptor duration and useful function are separate questions. Conditioning, repeat dosing, safety and total cost belong to a specified product and protocol rather than to the in vivo label.

Rurik used targeted mRNA lipid nanoparticles to generate transient CAR T cells in a mouse cardiac-injury model. It demonstrates a delivery/expression approach in that setting; it does not establish cancer efficacy, human safety or an interchangeable regimen for other delivery formats.

The INT2104 registry NCT06539338 identifies a phase 1 B-cell-cancer study in the dated source check. A trial design or registry listing does not supply efficacy results, prove local slot availability or validate a platform-wide claim about conditioning.

A prepared carrier can engineer the recipient's own cells. Vector or nanoparticle dose, ongoing delivery, newly generated cells, cell proliferation and receptor persistence should be measured separately. Stopping carrier administration need not immediately end the activity of cells already engineered.

The cited preclinical results do not by themselves establish a fixed cost reduction, universal absence of lymphodepletion or automatic repeat-dose feasibility. Evaluate the actual process, monitoring and protocol rather than treating these as inherent benefits of all in vivo products.

Ex vivo describes engineering outside the body followed by administration of a cell product. In vivo engineering administers an instruction-carrying product and generates modified cells inside the body; it is not the same as testing an ex vivo product in an animal. Location, recipient versus donor origin and transient versus stable genetic fate are separate attributes.

In a fictional sampled population of 200 cells, 60 show the stated receptor measurement: 60/200 is 30% of that sampled population at that time. It does not specify a whole-body engineered-cell count, the administered carrier dose, tissue distribution, durable expression or killing. Sequence detection, expression, abundance and biological function need their own measurements.

Hunter's 2025 study used targeted mRNA nanoparticles in healthy-donor and autoimmune patient cell samples, humanised mice and cynomolgus monkeys. Tumour control in mice and B-cell depletion in monkeys are not human treatment outcomes. Quality testing of the administered carrier also cannot sample every subsequently engineered cell or tissue; relevant biodistribution, expression, kinetics and safety evidence is still needed.

strengths: Investigates an alternative to administering cells engineered outside the body
May reduce some separate ex vivo manufacturing steps in a specified process
limitations: Cell targeting, off-target engineering and immune responses require measurement
Instruction dose does not specify final cell number or functional exposure
Conditioning, repeat dosing and cost are product- and protocol-specific

records.name: Cellular kinetics and persistence
records.tldr: A living cell therapy can change its number, location and state after administration. The starting dose, a sampled cell count and useful function are different measurements.
records.summary: After a cell infusion, measured abundance depends on division, survival and redistribution. In vivo engineering may also continue to generate newly engineered cells. A blood sample describes one compartment and time; it cannot count all cells in the body or establish entry into a tumor. Detectable receptor-encoding sequences, viable receptor-positive cells, persistent markers and functional activity should be reported separately.

A sequence assay is not automatically a count of viable cells expressing a functional surface receptor.

Keep the measurement method, time, compartment, units and denominator attached. A receptor-positive percentage can fall while absolute receptor-positive cells per microliter remain unchanged if the sampled denominator increases. Neither measure alone establishes an unchanged total-body cell population, tumor entry or antitumor benefit.

An administered cell dose is an input. The dose of a vector or particle used for in vivo engineering does not directly specify the later number of engineered cells. Autologous means the recipient’s own cells; allogeneic means cells from another person. Engineering outside versus inside the body is a separate axis; a prepared delivery product can engineer the recipient's own cells.

Expansion and persistence can prolong useful activity or harmful recognition. Stopping further administration does not instantly remove living cells or reverse an injury already triggered. A safety switch addresses a specified control mechanism; cell elimination, receptor shutoff and treatment of downstream inflammation are different interventions.

In the Liu cord-blood CAR-NK study, low-level detection at least 12 months after treatment belonged to a construct with IL-15 and an inducible caspase-9 switch. It does not establish the behavior of every NK-cell source or equate marker detection with continuing useful function.

records.name: Control of cell payloads by endogenous promoters
records.tldr: An engineered cell can place a payload under the control of a naturally regulated gene. The resulting expression pattern still needs measurement in the actual cells and tissues.
records.summary: A CRISPR knock-in can connect an engineered cytokine payload to regulatory control at an endogenous gene locus. In preclinical work, NR4A2 and RGS16 control supported cytokine expression in specified CAR T-cell settings, with tumor and safety measurements in mouse models. This is distinct from adding synthetic response elements to a separate promoter. Neither the locus name nor an activation-responsive design proves tumor-only secretion, clinical safety or patient benefit.

Patient-derived cells were also studied experimentally; that is not a clinical treatment result in those patients. The edited locus, retained native gene function, off-state expression, inducibility and persistence need characterization.

Guo and colleagues instead tested a synthetic NR4A-responsive promoter against a conventional NFAT-responsive promoter in human-cell experiments with weak stimulation. Reporter expression and improved proliferation in that system do not establish a clinical potency or safety ranking, and the synthetic promoter is distinct from an endogenous NR4A2-locus knock-in.

Keep trigger recognition, payload transcription, secretion, tissue distribution and downstream activity separate. The IL-12 TIL clinical experience shows why inducible production alone cannot establish confinement or freedom from systemic toxicity. Viable producer-cell abundance, time and cell state matter alongside cytokine concentration.

records.name: Cell-therapy safety switches
records.tldr: An engineered switch can control a specified cell activity or promote cell removal. Lower signaling, fewer living cells and reversal of injury are different outcomes.
records.summary:
A living cell product can persist after administration stops. Activity switches regulate a defined function; elimination switches aim to remove cells. A drug-gated receptor may require a supplied molecule for signaling, whereas inducible caspase-9 activates a cell-death pathway when its dimerizing trigger is given. A removable surface tag offers another clearance route. These mechanisms need evidence within the actual finished product, including trigger exposure, speed, completeness and residual activity. None guarantees instant removal from every tissue or reversal of prior injury.

Di Stasi tested inducible caspase-9 in donor T cells after haploidentical stem-cell transplantation, rather than as a general CAR-T rescue trial. In the GD2-CART01 neuroblastoma report, the suicide switch was activated in one participant.

The report describes a reduction exceeding 90% of modified T cells within half an hour and control of that disease. This is a specified transplant setting, not proof of complete whole-body clearance or reversal of every CAR-associated toxicity.

Wang described a truncated EGFR marker lacking ligand-binding regions and intracellular kinase activity while retaining a cetuximab-binding epitope. The cell-engineering report studied selection, tracking and antibody-mediated clearance. A drug having an approved use does not establish that every marker/antibody combination is a validated clinical rescue system.

Check baseline leakage, incomplete switch expression, survivors that regrow, and the trigger’s access to relevant tissues. Evaluate the switch after manufacture within the finished cell product; a sequence result cannot substitute for these functional tests.

records.principle: Name the controlled process and trigger, then measure receptor activity, viable engineered-cell abundance and downstream harms separately before and after triggering.
strengths: Additional control over a specified activity or a cell population in tested constructs
limitations: Some cells or functions can survive the trigger
Released mediators and tissue injury can persist after cells decline
Cell removal can also remove useful activity; trigger access and product quality matter

records.name: T-cell engagers (bispecific)
records.tldr: T-cell engagers are proteins that bind a specified target and recruit T cells, often through CD3. A binding bridge does not by itself establish completed killing.
records.summary:
A dosed T-cell engager supplies a protein connecting target recognition to an available T cell. It does not itself install receptor instructions or supply engineered living responders. Product design can use antibody-derived binding fragments or a soluble TCR recognition domain; some target arms require a particular peptide-HLA complex. Compact BiTE designs, Fc-containing architectures and half-life extension describe features that can overlap rather than mutually exclusive treatment categories.

Clinical examples include blinatumomab in B-cell precursor acute lymphoblastic leukemia, teclistamab in multiple myeloma and tarlatamab in extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer. Their actual labels define different settings, combinations, prior treatments and harms. Tebentafusp is a peptide-HLA-directed soluble TCR/CD3 protein with its own allele- and disease-specific use. Neither a common platform name nor binding in a laboratory establishes eligibility or comparative benefit.

notes: An antibody-derived TCR mimic recognizes a peptide-HLA complex using an antibody scaffold. A soluble TCR/CD3 engager instead uses a TCR-derived recognition scaffold attached to a recruiting arm. TCR-T administers cells carrying receptor chains. Target recognition, molecular scaffold and administered object are separate axes; a mimic can be part of an engager without becoming a TCR protein.

Liddy studied soluble TCR/CD3 ImmTAC proteins in experimental systems. Dao studied an antibody-derived WT1/HLA-A*02:01/CD3 engager in cells and mice. Their results do not establish clinical benefit for every scaffold, HLA allele or cancer. Recruiting another T cell does not require that cell’s native receptor to recognize the target, but does not remove the target arm’s HLA restriction.

The KIMMTRAK label identifies tebentafusp as a soluble gp100 peptide-HLA/CD3 protein for HLA-A*02:01-positive adults with unresectable or metastatic uveal melanoma. This is a named clinical protein example, not an engineered-cell product or evidence that other peptide-HLA binders share its indication or outcomes.

Binding to supplied peptide-HLA reagent can bypass natural processing and display. Source-protein expression or a compatible genotype alone is not a functional target assay. For a research claim, compare naturally presenting targets, irrelevant peptides, the wrong HLA allele, antigen-negative targets, suitable effector cells, no-effector conditions and healthy tissues. Labeled clinical selection tests remain a separate clinical-use rule. Record the peptide sequence, HLA allele, display method and its detection or recovery limits; no universal target-density cutoff follows from the format name.

The Mack construct joined two single-chain Fv fragments with a peptide linker in one compact protein; this is different from an IgG architecture with an Fc region. The FDA tarlatamab application describes DLL3/CD3 binding domains combined with an IgG Fc region in a half-life-extended BiTE. Thus BiTE, Fc-containing and half-life-extended are not three exclusive buckets. Fc design, binding geometry, affinity, target density, distribution and measured exposure still belong to the specific molecule. The Giffin cell, mouse and nonhuman-primate study does not define a universal human schedule.

Compare recognition, T-cell activation, proliferation, target death, cytokine release and protein exposure at named times. Record effector source/state, target density, effector-to-target ratio, dose or concentration and denominator; include target-negative and no-effector controls. A granule or cytokine signal does not substitute for completed target-cell death or clinical benefit. Cytokines in a culture are a measured laboratory endpoint, not a diagnosis of clinical cytokine-release syndrome.

Bluemel compared epitope positions and antigen sizes in engineered cell systems. Constructs with similar target-binding affinity differed in target-cell lysis, supporting functional testing of the actual geometry rather than ranking every molecule by affinity alone. In the solitomab phase 1 solid-tumor study, dose-limiting diarrhea and liver abnormalities constrained dose escalation; an accessible target and a binding bridge did not by themselves establish a useful therapeutic window.

Compared with administered CAR-T or TCR-T cells, a protein engager recruits effectors rather than supplying engineered responders. Protein mass/concentration and viable-cell dose have different units; clearance differs from cell survival, expansion and trafficking. A shared target name does not establish matched epitope, affinity, contact geometry, exposure, controllability or safety.

The 2025 FDA tarlatamab decision followed the randomized DeLLphi-304 comparison after platinum-based treatment in SCLC. Its survival finding belongs to that drug and setting. The cited blinatumomab consolidation and teclistamab combination/monotherapy decisions likewise retain their own settings; none is a class-wide treatment-sequencing rule.

For a lymphoma engager, target presence, access to suitable T cells and useful effector function need separate evidence. Antigen expression alone does not establish these other steps. These biological questions do not by themselves select an earlier treatment line; treatment timing needs evidence for the actual drug and setting.
records.principle: A specified target-binding region and T-cell-recruiting region promote encounters. CD3 recruitment can bypass the recruited cell’s own antigen specificity; a peptide-HLA-binding target arm still retains its peptide and HLA requirements.
strengths: Established clinical uses for particular products in defined settings
Protein exposure can be adjusted through a specified dosing regimen
limitations: Productive encounters need accessible targets and functional effectors
Healthy-tissue recognition, cytokine release and neurologic harms need product-specific evidence
Stopping administration does not instantly clear protein or reverse an effect already triggered

records.name: TCR-T cell therapy
records.tldr: TCR-T supplies living T cells carrying a selected receptor that recognizes a specified peptide with its presenting HLA molecule. A source-protein name alone does not establish that target.
records.summary:
Conventional alpha-beta TCR-T introduces selected paired receptor-chain instructions into therapeutic T cells. The receptor recognizes a displayed peptide-HLA complex, rather than entering the tumor cell to bind the whole source protein. Natural processing, the required HLA allele, surface display, receptor expression and useful cell function remain different questions. This differs from administering a soluble TCR/CD3 protein that recruits other T cells.

Afamitresgene autoleucel (Tecelra) is an approved TCR-T example. FDA initially approved it in 2024 and converted the specified adult use to traditional approval in June 2026, extending the indication to patients aged 12 and older. Its synovial-sarcoma indication retains prior-chemotherapy, selected HLA and MAGE-A4 testing requirements. The full label also contains exclusions and safety requirements; a broad HLA-A*02 label is not a complete eligibility rule.

notes: Morgan transferred receptor genes into autologous lymphocytes in a metastatic-melanoma study. Introducing selected recognition instructions differs from expanding a tumor-derived population with its existing receptors. Viral transduction describes a delivery method, not the definition of every receptor-engineering process.

The conventional receptor uses paired alpha and beta chains alongside the CD3 complex. Cloning selected receptor coding sequences means copying instructions; one sequenced chain does not establish a complete functional receptor or its specificity. Expression and assembly in the finished cells require evaluation. The Dong structural study distinguishes recognition chains from associated signaling components. Bendle showed in mouse models that introduced and endogenous chains could form self-reactive mixed receptors; vector and cell-population changes reduced that model risk. This does not supply a clinical risk rate for every TCR-T product.

Protein expression and HLA typing lie upstream of the displayed ligand. Antigen/HLA loss or impaired presentation can remove one recognition route; retaining another allele does not rescue a receptor requiring the lost allele. A different receptor using a retained allele needs its own specificity and functional evidence.

In research, test paired receptor expression and naturally presenting targets, with relevant antigen/HLA removal and restoration, irrelevant peptides, unmodified effectors and healthy tissue. Multimer or peptide-loaded reagent binding is different from natural processing, target-cell death or patient benefit. This research validation is distinct from the approved product’s clinical testing rule.

Cameron investigated fatal cardiac toxicity with one affinity-enhanced MAGE-A3 receptor and identified a cross-reactive Titin peptide presented by HLA-A*01 as the most likely cause. Earlier screening had not detected the hazard. This was a different receptor from the MAGE-A4 product Tecelra; stronger binding does not establish improved specificity or safety for either a new construct or an entire family.

The June 2026 Tecelra label names HLA-A*02:01P, -A*02:02P, -A*02:03P and -A*02:06P and a MAGE-A4 tumor test in its indication, with a separate HLA-A*02:05P contraindication. The approval letter documents the adult conversion and pediatric expansion. These are product-specific regulatory scopes, not a general rule for every TCR-T.

Conventional surface-antigen CARs and peptide-HLA-directed receptors have different recognition requirements, but peptide-HLA CARs also exist. The WT1/HLA-A*24:02 CAR study is a preclinical counterexample to saying all intracellular source antigens are unreachable by any CAR. A format change does not supply a missing required peptide-HLA complex.

For a soluble TCR/CD3 protein, the dosed molecule supplies recognition and recruits available T cells. TCR-T instead supplies receptor-bearing living cells. Protein exposure, cell trafficking/persistence and useful target-dependent function need separate measurements; neither format wins by definition.
records.principle: Selected alpha-beta recognition chains operate with the cell’s CD3 signaling machinery. The intended target is the particular naturally displayed peptide-HLA complex, not genotype, RNA abundance or source protein alone.
strengths: Can investigate targets derived from intracellular proteins through peptide-HLA display
A selected receptor can confer recognition on engineered cells in defined settings
limitations: Allele and antigen-processing/display dependencies can limit recognition
Cross-reactivity, healthy-tissue recognition and whole-regimen harms require evaluation
Receptor-positive cells still need appropriate state, tissue access and function

records.name: TIL therapy
records.tldr: TIL therapy expands lymphocytes collected from a tumor and returns a prepared cell product. Tissue origin, culture yield and useful tumor recognition are different claims.
records.summary:
Tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte therapy starts with cells collected from tumor tissue, commonly using their existing T-cell receptors. Infiltration does not prove that every cell recognizes the cancer. Culture and selection can change which clones become abundant; final viable-cell yield, recognition breadth and useful function need their own evidence. Manufacturing, conditioning, cytokine support and follow-up form a complete regimen with separate contributions and harms.

Lifileucel (Amtagvi) received accelerated FDA approval in 2024 for specified previously treated unresectable or metastatic melanoma. Its label defines the prior-treatment conditions and regimen. TILVANCE-301 is a phase 3 advanced-melanoma study of a lifileucel regimen with pembrolizumab versus pembrolizumab. Neither a registry design nor clinical evidence from one TIL process establishes benefit for every tumor or manufacturing method.

Its CD39 observations belong to those sampled populations, not a universal marker rule that proves the specificity of every manufactured cell.

Conventional alpha-beta T cells recognize peptide-HLA targets. A mixed TIL product can contain multiple specificities, but breadth must be tested against relevant naturally presenting targets and lesions. Polyclonality does not guarantee freedom from antigen/presentation escape or other resistance.

Record input tissue, culture/selection conditions, viable-cell yield, identity and the final receptor mixture. An expanding bystander clone can increase total yield while reducing the proportion with useful tumor recognition. A receptor repertoire measured before culture is not automatically the infusion product’s repertoire.

A pathology infiltration estimate describes a tissue feature under a specified scoring rule; it is not the viable-cell count recovered for manufacture, a dose, or proof of tumor reactivity. Functional studies need target material, HLA/antigen controls, suitable effectors, timing, units and readout context. Binding, target death and clinical outcome remain different endpoints.

Rohaan randomized patients with advanced melanoma to a specified TIL regimen or ipilimumab. In the reported intention-to-treat population, median progression-free survival was 7.2 versus 3.1 months. The TIL arm included lymphodepleting chemotherapy and high-dose IL-2; grade 3 or higher events in that arm were mainly chemotherapy-related myelosuppression. This comparison concerns the whole regimen and is not the lifileucel registration dataset or an isolated test of cells alone.

FDA’s Amtagvi source describes an autologous tumor-derived product and a defined previously treated melanoma use. The label requires conditioning and post-infusion IL-2 and carries serious regimen warnings. A manufacturing success, a registry listing or a positive cellular assay is not an independent clinical-benefit claim for another process or cancer. Its label lists the specific mechanism of action as unknown. General TIL recognition biology does not establish which clones or components explain an individual response.

The NCT05727904 registry identifies TILVANCE-301 as a randomized phase 3 study in untreated advanced melanoma, with a lifileucel/conditioning/IL-2 regimen plus pembrolizumab compared with pembrolizumab. The registry description does not supply an efficacy result or local availability for a participant.

TIL describes tissue origin, while added receptor or other genetic engineering describes an additional property. Experimental engineering can overlap that origin category; neither name implies the other. Tumor entry before collection also does not guarantee trafficking or useful persistence after transfer.
records.principle: Recover tumor-derived lymphocytes, expand or select them through a specified process, characterize the final cells and evaluate the complete treatment regimen in its disease setting.
strengths: Can investigate multiple naturally occurring recognition specificities
Clinical evidence exists for specified melanoma products and regimens
limitations: Usable tissue and suitable manufacture are required
Bystander cells and culture selection can limit useful recognition
Conditioning, cytokine support, cell infusion and follow-up have their own risks and access requirements

records.name: Bispecific antibodies
records.tldr: A bispecific antibody has two binding specificities. They can recognize different antigens or different parts of one antigen; the finished molecule can have more than two binding sites.
records.summary:
Bispecific describes recognition, rather than one required shape or biological action. Some molecules bridge a target cell to an immune effector. Others engage two targets or two epitopes without bridging two cells. Antibody fragments, IgG-based structures and added binding domains can arrange these specificities differently. A T-cell engager is one functional use; a conjugated payload is another product feature.

Two specificities do not establish that both targets are reached together, that binding produces killing, or that a molecule improves on a comparison treatment. Function, exposure, manufacturing quality and harms need evidence for the actual product and indication. A class containing approved drugs does not make every bispecific design an approved therapy.

notes: Specificity counts what is recognized; valency counts binding sites. Two different epitopes on the same antigen can provide two specificities. Added sites do not necessarily add a new specificity, and one molecule is different from separately dosed antibodies.

FDA guidance distinguishes products that bridge two cells from products whose functions do not require that bridge. Some mechanisms require both target interactions at the same time; others do not. Do not assume that every bispecific recruits T cells or that every target pair acts as an AND gate.

The manufacturing evaluation includes molecular identity, correct pairing, aggregation, fragments, stability and biological potency. Affinity, binding kinetics, avidity, target distribution and exposure belong to the actual format. Two successful binding assays do not by themselves demonstrate the intended combined function.

CD20/CD3 lymphoma engagers illustrate one bispecific format: CD20 recognition connects to T-cell recruitment through CD3. The target-binding step does not require tumor peptide-HLA recognition, but that does not guarantee useful cell function or response. Cytokine release syndrome and neurologic toxicity do not demonstrate effective tumor killing; step-up dosing is product-specific risk management, not freedom from serious harm.
records.principle: Describe each recognition site, its epitope and copy number, then test whether simultaneous binding is needed for the intended effect in the relevant biological setting.
strengths: Can place two recognition functions within a defined molecule
Different formats can be tested for a particular intended mechanism
limitations: Binding-site geometry and exposure can change function
Healthy tissues can carry either recognized target
Additional specificities do not establish greater benefit or freedom from harm

records.name: Tarlatamab
records.tldr: Tarlatamab is a DLL3/CD3 T-cell-engaging protein approved for extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer progressing on or after platinum chemotherapy.
records.summary:
Tarlatamab connects DLL3 recognition to recruitment through CD3. FDA initially granted accelerated approval in 2024 and granted traditional approval in November 2025 after the randomized DeLLphi-304 comparison with chemotherapy. Its labeled use is extensive-stage SCLC progressing on or after platinum-based chemotherapy; findings from an earlier response study and the later survival comparison belong to different trials.

CRS and neurologic toxicity, including ICANS, remain boxed warnings. The September 2026 label specifies 6-to-8-hour monitoring in an appropriate healthcare setting on cycle 1 days 1 and 8, next-day assessments and further caregiver/proximity instructions. Dose step-up, interruptions and toxicity management follow the full current label; the protein format does not guarantee an immediately reversible effect.

records.name: DeLLphi-301: tarlatamab, a DLL3-targeting T-cell engager, in previously treated small-cell lung cancer
records.tldr: In the phase 2 DeLLphi-301 study, tarlatamab produced an objective response in 40% of the evaluated 10-mg group. This study did not compare it with standard chemotherapy.
records.summary:
DeLLphi-301 was an open-label phase 2 study of tarlatamab, a DLL3/CD3 T-cell-engaging protein, in previously treated small-cell lung cancer. The publication reports 220 treated patients, with 10-mg and 100-mg dose groups. Blinded independent central review assessed objective response.

At the reported cutoff, objective response was 40% in the 10-mg group and 32% in the 100-mg group. Median progression-free survival was 4.9 and 3.9 months, respectively. The abstract reports estimated survival at 9 months, rather than a mature median overall-survival comparison with chemotherapy. The later DeLLphi-304 randomized chemotherapy comparison is a separate study, reflected in FDA’s 2025 traditional-approval decision.

findings: Objective response: 40% (97.5% CI 29 to 52) in the 10-mg group and 32% (97.5% CI 21 to 44) in the 100-mg group.

The later FDA traditional approval concerns extensive-stage disease progressing on or after platinum chemotherapy. CRS and neurologic toxicity remain serious risks. The September 2026 label specifies 6-to-8-hour monitoring in an appropriate healthcare setting on cycle 1 days 1 and 8, with next-day assessments and further caregiver/proximity instructions; the full current label governs the regimen.
caveats: Randomized dose allocation is different from randomization against standard chemotherapy. DeLLphi-304 supplies the later chemotherapy comparison.

Response duration among responders, progression-free survival and overall survival have different endpoints and denominators. Results at one cutoff do not establish superiority to every earlier treatment.

records.name: C-144-01: lifileucel, tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes grown from a patient's own tumour, in melanoma after checkpoint inhibitors have failed
records.tldr: The reported 66-person phase 2 lifileucel cohort had a 36% objective response rate after prior checkpoint therapy. It tested a complete TIL regimen without a randomized comparator.
records.summary:
This open-label, single-arm phase 2 report evaluated centrally manufactured lifileucel in advanced melanoma after checkpoint treatment. Sixty-six patients received lymphodepletion, a single lifileucel infusion and up to six high-dose IL-2 doses. The abstract reports a mean of 3.3 prior therapies, not a median. Investigator-assessed objective response was the primary endpoint.

Objective response was 36% (95% CI 25 to 49), comprising two complete and 22 partial responses. Median response duration had not been reached at 18.7 months of median follow-up. These are the reported cohort and cutoff; they are separate from later pooled analyses and the FDA regulatory analysis.

records.name: TROP2
records.tldr: TROP2 is a surface protein found in normal epithelial cells and many cancers. It is used to deliver antibody-drug conjugates and has biological signalling roles; those observations do not establish an individual tumour’s response.

Experimental studies have also linked wild-type TROP2 expression and signalling to growth in defined cell and animal models. Its delivery role, biological function, possible genomic alterations and clinical treatment-selection rules are separate questions. The current U.S. breast-cancer indications of these two ADCs do not require a TROP2 expression test, while other disease, prior-treatment and regimen-specific criteria still apply.

records.name: TROP2 expression
records.tldr: TROP2 expression is a measured feature, not a universal ADC selection rule. The current U.S. breast-cancer uses of sacituzumab govitecan and datopotamab deruxtecan do not require a TROP2 test; other treatment requirements still apply.
records.summary:
In ASCENT, a prespecified exploratory analysis used an immunohistochemical H-score to examine TROP2 expression. Results were available for 290 of the 468 patients in the primary population without brain metastases. The authors supported benefit in the high and medium groups and said the low group was too small for a definitive benefit conclusion. This analysis does not establish equal effects at every expression level or a validated universal threshold. A marker association, a randomised treatment comparison and a treatment-by-marker interaction answer different questions.

The current U.S. breast indications for sacituzumab govitecan and datopotamab deruxtecan do not require a TROP2 selection assay. That regulatory rule does not prove that the target or its delivery is biologically irrelevant. Check the exact drug, subtype, setting and prior treatment. The first-line sacituzumab-pembrolizumab regimen has a separate PD-L1 CPS requirement of at least 10 using an FDA-authorized test. A research H-score or computational membrane score is not automatically an interchangeable clinical selection test.

records.tldr: ASCENT compared sacituzumab govitecan with single-agent chemotherapy in previously treated metastatic triple-negative breast cancer. The primary analysis excluded patients with brain metastases.
records.summary:
ASCENT (NCT02574455), published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2021, randomised 529 patients overall. The primary population comprised 468 without brain metastases. Sacituzumab govitecan improved progression-free and overall survival compared with physician’s-choice single-agent chemotherapy in that population. A prespecified exploratory biomarker analysis had TROP2 data for 290 of the 468 primary-population patients. The authors supported benefit in the high and medium groups and considered the low group too small for a definitive conclusion. The absence of a TROP2 label-selection requirement is a separate regulatory fact. Post hoc demographic and brain-metastasis analyses retain their own populations and uncertainty; none is a prospective validation of a universal marker cutoff.

records.name: HER2 testing in the UK: reflex ISH, the ratio against the copy number, and where the UK differs from ASCO/CAP
records.tldr: Breast HER2 interpretation depends on the assay, scoring system and guideline. UK and U.S. guidance differ in some uncommon ISH cases; the concurrent protein-staining result matters.
records.summary:
RCPath G148 version 3, dated November 2024, describes UK breast HER2 testing with immunohistochemistry followed by ISH for equivocal cases, or an ISH approach in specified circumstances. The September 2026 CAP template also records no detected membrane staining separately from faint membrane staining within the historical IHC 0 band. A reporting convention is different from a product-specific clinical indication, and neither a raw count nor a staining score alone establishes an individual treatment decision.

records.name: Thermal ablation (RFA, microwave, cryo)
records.tldr: Thermal ablation uses an applicator to heat or freeze selected tissue. Safe coverage and later local control need assessment beyond placing the device.
records.summary:
Image-guided thermal ablation includes radiofrequency current, microwave fields and cryoablation. The applicator changes tissue temperature; injury depends on exposure through space and time. Chemical ablation and membrane-disrupting electrical approaches belong to a broader ablation category and should be named separately. These methods differ from ionising radiation.

Planning considers access, the target and intended margin, blood flow and nearby structures. Neither a central reading nor a visible treatment zone proves lethal exposure throughout the target. A study’s lesion-size rule is not a universal physical ceiling. Treatment can injure normal tissue and may require further procedures; outpatient treatment, preserved function and unlimited repeatability are not guaranteed.

The reporting consensus separates technical coverage, technique efficacy at a defined follow-up and later local progression. The method, assessment, retreatments and complications belong with each result. Local control or symptom relief does not establish eradication of disease elsewhere or a systemic immune benefit.

The historical mechanistic literature emphasises temperature, time, thawing and repetition; a probe setpoint is not exposure everywhere in the tissue. Georgiades and colleagues studied normal renal tissue in swine. Measurements from six test animals found a mean nonlethal rim of 0.75 millimetres, with variation and widening near large vessels. Their proposed six-millimetre visible-ice margin for renal cancer was an extrapolation under stated assumptions, rather than a measured universal human margin.

Site, geometry, applicators and nearby structures affect feasibility and harm. Freezing, preserved material or local tissue destruction alone does not establish antigen presentation, useful immune priming or distant tumour control.

records.name: SBRT / SABR (stereotactic radiotherapy)
records.tldr: Stereotactic body radiotherapy delivers a high dose per treatment to a defined body target using specialised localisation and verification. A short schedule alone does not identify it or establish safety.
records.summary:
Stereotactic body radiotherapy, also called SABR, uses specialised localisation, planning, positioning, image guidance and delivery to give a high dose per fraction to a body target outside the brain. A small number of visits does not establish that this delivery package was used. A biologically effective dose calculation compares modelled effects under assumptions; it does not document stereotactic localisation, motion management or verification. Modern non-stereotactic radiotherapy can also use imaging, conformal beams and motion assessment.

The target, motion, dose distribution, positioning uncertainty, prior overlapping radiation and normal-organ constraints determine the coverage problem. Dose falls through space rather than stopping at a drawn line. There is no universal one-centimetre safe boundary, lesion-size ceiling or prescription that applies to every organ. Planned exposure, verified delivery, local control and toxicity need their own measurements.

A 2010 prospective study concerned medically inoperable peripheral early-stage lung cancer and measured local control, distant failure and toxicity. That setting does not validate treatment of every central lesion or organ. CURB and NRG-BR002 tested different metastatic settings and comparisons. Local control, added progression-free or overall survival, symptom relief and an immune response are separate outcomes.

Planned exposure, verified delivery, local control and toxicity need their own measurements.

A 2010 prospective study concerned medically inoperable peripheral early-stage lung cancer and measured local control, distant failure and toxicity. That setting does not validate treatment of every central lesion or organ. CURB and NRG-BR002 tested different metastatic settings and comparisons. Local control, added progression-free or overall survival, symptom relief and an immune response are separate outcomes.
