records.name: Radiotherapy
records.tldr: Radiotherapy deposits ionising radiation in tissue to damage cancer cells. The target, normal tissues, treatment schedule and clinical goal all matter.
records.summary:
Radiation transfers energy to tissue and can damage DNA directly or through reactive molecules. Cells can repair damage or lose their ability to keep dividing, and death can occur later. One treatment session is an exposure, rather than an immediate count of dead cells. Oxygen, cell state and repair affect the response.

External beams, brachytherapy sources and systemically distributed radiopharmaceuticals have different exposure patterns. An external-beam target can include tissue at risk of microscopic disease after surgery, even when no mass is visible. Planning and verification consider geometry, motion, normal organs and previous overlapping exposure. Precision does not eliminate normal-tissue dose or injury.

Absorbed dose in gray is energy per mass: one gray is one joule per kilogram. Total dose, fraction size, timing and exposed volume influence biological effects. Physical-dose arithmetic alone does not establish equivalence of schedules. Local or regional control, symptom relief, distant disease and survival remain distinct clinical outcomes.

records.name: Hypofractionation (fewer, larger radiotherapy doses)
records.tldr: Hypofractionation uses larger radiation doses per treatment than a specified comparison schedule, usually with fewer treatments. Control and harms depend on the whole tested regimen.
records.summary:
Hypofractionation uses larger doses per fraction relative to a stated conventional comparison, commonly with fewer treatments. Keep total gray, dose per fraction, count, spacing, overall duration and treatment volume together. For equal fractions, total physical dose is the fraction count multiplied by dose per fraction; this arithmetic does not establish biological equivalence. Acceleration changes overall timing; a boost changes the dose to a selected region. Hypofractionation does not by itself identify stereotactic delivery.

Biological response depends on tissue, repair and timing, rather than total physical dose alone. Alpha/beta is a model parameter in gray describing fraction-size sensitivity. Under the linear-quadratic model and its assumptions, a lower ratio predicts greater sensitivity to fraction size at the same total physical dose. Historical teaching values near 10 gray for early effects and 3 for late effects are conventions, not universal constants. A planned START-A/pilot meta-analysis estimated 4.6 gray for tumour control, with confidence interval 1.1 to 8.1, and 3.4 for late photographic breast change, with interval 2.3 to 4.5. Keep the model, endpoint and uncertainty.

START-B compared 50 gray in 25 fractions over five weeks with 40 in 15 over three weeks after surgery for early breast cancer, assessing local-regional relapse and late effects. FAST-Forward tested 40 gray in 15 fractions over three weeks against 27 or 26 in five over one week to the whole breast or chest wall. Its five-year report supported non-inferiority of 26 gray for breast relapse under the trial margin; 27 gray produced more normal-tissue effects. These results do not validate every five-visit course, nodal field, reirradiation plan or immune-priming schedule.

records.name: Immunogenic cell death
records.tldr: Immunogenic cell death is regulated cell death that can initiate adaptive immunity against the dying cells in a suitable host and context. Injury alone does not establish it.
records.summary:
The 2020 consensus defines immunogenic cell death through the adaptive immune response, not merely the appearance of dead cells. Antigens, appropriately timed danger signals, antigen-presenting cells and a responsive host all matter. Apoptotic or other death machinery does not by itself classify the immune outcome.

Calreticulin exposure, ATP or HMGB1 release and interferon-related signals are useful mechanistic readouts, but none alone proves protective immunity. Functional cross-priming and appropriate in-vivo immune tests address later steps. The consensus distinguishes mouse vaccination models from established disease; neither a surrogate marker nor a positive mouse assay establishes clinical benefit in a person.

Immunogenic cell death is regulated death capable of initiating antigen-specific adaptive immunity in a compatible responding host. Antigenicity and appropriately timed adjuvant signals are both necessary considerations. It is an immune consequence, not an exclusive machine opposed to apoptosis or necrotic appearance.

Surface calreticulin, released ATP and HMGB1 have distinct mechanistic roles in defined experiments. Calreticulin supported dying-cell uptake, ATP signalled through dendritic-cell P2X7/inflammasome pathways, and HMGB1/TLR4 supported processing and presentation. These are examples rather than a universal sufficient three-marker checklist. A DAMP is not automatically a tumour-specific antigen.

In the consensus vaccination assay, remove residual inducing chemical and add no separate adjuvant before vaccinating immunocompetent syngeneic mice with dying tumour cells. Compare later challenge with living matched tumour cells in vaccinated and unvaccinated hosts, and test specificity with unrelated compatible tumour cells. Incidence and growth are functional readouts. Immune-competent versus deficient comparisons alone cannot isolate immunogenic death from other immunostimulation. Assays consume tumour-cell aliquots, supernatant or host-model material and report separate dead-cell fractions, signal concentrations or surface staining and challenge incidence or growth. Residual inducer, contamination, incompatible antigens and poor death confirmation can invalidate attribution. No universal DAMP cutoff establishes immunogenicity.

Death plus extracellular ATP does not establish a cancer vaccine. Danger signals, cross-priming, functional protection, distant control and patient benefit are separate claims. Even a positive mouse vaccination assay remains model-bound and does not select a clinical treatment.

records.name: In situ vaccination
records.tldr: In situ vaccination aims to use antigens at a tumour site to stimulate useful immune recognition. Local destruction does not automatically make the tumour a successful vaccine.
records.summary:
Local treatment can supply tumour antigens, and an adjuvant or other immune intervention may support their presentation and priming. The proposal needs evidence for each step and for useful immune effects in the relevant host and setting. It does not guarantee recognition of every antigen or every lesion.

Injury, danger signals, immune-cell changes, distant lesion responses and comparative patient outcomes are different observations. The actual local method and accompanying treatments must be named. A response during combined treatment does not isolate which component caused it.

Antigen availability, uptake and processing, cross-presentation, suitable priming, access to another lesion, recognition of naturally displayed targets and useful function are conditional jobs. Local injury can supply material without establishing all these steps, and danger signals alone do not establish immunogenic cell death. An uninjected lesion can still be exposed to systemic drugs.

Intratumoral immunotherapy describes a delivery route and treatment purpose; in-situ vaccination describes a proposed learning strategy. Not every injected cytotoxic or immune-directed treatment is a vaccine. Local shrinkage, antigen-reactive blood responses, distant control and longer-term clinical benefit are different outcomes, and a multicomponent result does not isolate each component’s contribution.

Brody’s early study combined low-dose radiation and an injected CpG TLR9 agonist in 15 people with low-grade B-cell lymphoma. Hammerich combined Flt3 ligand, radiation and the TLR3 agonist poly-ICLC in indolent lymphoma with accompanying models. The latter report’s restored sensitivity to PD-1 blockade was demonstrated in mice; it is not established human combination benefit or evidence for every injection or a breast-cancer regimen.

Assessment combines local sampling, controlled immune assays and serial treated/uninjected-lesion measurements. Tissue, blood and viable cells are finite inputs. Keep local change, specified reactive-cell counts or functions, and response proportions under their stated rules separate. No universal marker proves successful vaccination. Nonspecific inflammation, added peptide, viability, missed sampling times and concurrent therapy can confound results; a model or assay needs separate clinical validation of the complete intervention.

Added peptide can bypass natural processing. Appropriate naturally presenting targets and recognition or cytotoxicity controls address a separate bridge, within the model’s limits. In a fictional study, the injected lesion shrinks and blood cells respond to supplied tumour peptides, while another lesion is unchanged. Local activity and assay reactivity were observed; natural recognition, access and useful distant function remain unproven. The unchanged lesion also does not establish absence of every immune-learning event.

records.name: Abscopal effect
records.tldr: An abscopal response is regression outside an irradiated area, studied as a possible systemic effect of local radiation. Observing it does not by itself establish the cause or an added survival benefit.
records.summary:
Responses at non-irradiated sites motivate investigation of immune effects of local radiation. Keep the irradiated and unirradiated lesions, other treatments and observation times explicit. A proposed immune mechanism needs more than local injury or circulating markers.

A case or uncontrolled combination cannot isolate the added effect of radiation. Comparative local-treatment studies must retain their populations and endpoints: a response outside the field, progression-free survival, overall survival and symptom relief are different outcomes.

Demaria’s bilateral 67NR mammary-tumour mouse experiment combined local radiation with Flt3 ligand. The distant tumour grew more slowly under the combination, whereas radiation alone affected the irradiated tumour; antigen-mismatched and T-cell-deficient comparisons supported an immune-dependent component. This is a defined combined animal intervention, not a human response rate. Postow’s ipilimumab-plus-radiation melanoma report was one case with temporal immune correlates, not a study of frequency.

Formenti enrolled 39 people with chemotherapy-refractory metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer in a single-arm radiation-plus-ipilimumab study. At day 88, 21 had completed treatment and response assessment. Seven responses were 7/39, about 18% of those enrolled, or 7/21, about 33% of those evaluable. These denominators answer different questions and neither estimates radiation-alone activity or an individual breast-cancer response probability.

Report lesion changes separately from patient response proportions and their eligible denominators. Imaging is an input; optional tissue and immune tests use finite samples. There is no universal abscopal cutoff or percentage across cancers and regimens; case observations, model mechanisms and comparative clinical outcomes are different evidence tiers.

In a fictional combination study, an irradiated site is controlled while a lesion outside the field shrinks during systemic therapy. The observation is a distant response under that treatment context. It does not prove that radiation vaccinated the whole body, establish which component caused it or supply a general response frequency. Test exposure, relevant comparisons and the proposed immune mechanism separately.

records.name: Systemic versus local therapy
records.tldr: Local and regional treatments act in selected anatomical areas; systemic treatments circulate more broadly. The route does not guarantee adequate exposure or cancer control at every site.
records.summary:
Surgery, ablation and external radiation address defined tissues, while systemically administered medicines and radiopharmaceuticals distribute more broadly. Regional delivery has an intermediate anatomical scope. Distribution, effective exposure and benefit are separate questions; neither local nor systemic is a guarantee of complete cellular coverage.

Local control, distant progression, progression-free survival, overall survival and symptom relief should be measured separately. A null added-survival comparison does not make palliation irrelevant, and a controlled treated site does not establish control throughout the body. Compare the actual complete strategies rather than assuming that adding a local method always improves outcomes.

Breast cancer, the long-term comparison with mastectomy. In the Milan trial, 701 women with breast cancers no larger than 2 cm were randomly assigned between 1973 and 1980 to radical (Halsted) mastectomy (349) or quadrantectomy followed by radiotherapy (352). After a median 20 years of follow-up, death from any cause had occurred in 41.2 percent of the radical mastectomy group and 41.7 percent of the conserving surgery group (P equals 1.0), and death from breast cancer in 24.3 and 26.1 percent (P equals 0.8). What differed was the breast: 30 women in the conserving group had a recurrence in the same breast against 8 local recurrences after radical mastectomy, a crude cumulative incidence of 8.8 against 2.3 percent, with no significant difference in contralateral cancers, distant metastases or second primary cancers.

In NSABP B-06, 1,851 women were randomly assigned to total mastectomy, lumpectomy alone, or lumpectomy with breast irradiation, and followed for 20 years. Recurrence in the same breast occurred in 14.3 percent of those given radiotherapy against 39.2 percent of those not (P less than 0.001), and no significant difference was found between the three groups in disease-free survival, distant-disease-free survival or overall survival: the hazard ratio for death was 1.05 (0.90 to 1.23) for lumpectomy alone against total mastectomy and 0.97 (0.83 to 1.14) for lumpectomy with irradiation.

NICE NG101 (1.13.3) says to offer whole-breast radiotherapy to women with invasive breast cancer who have had breast-conserving surgery with clear margins, and (1.13.4, 1.13.5) to consider partial-breast radiotherapy for women aged 50 and over with tumours 3 cm or less that are N0, ER-positive, HER2-negative and grade 1 to 2 who will take endocrine therapy for at least 5 years, telling them that local recurrence at 5 years is equivalent, that the risk beyond 5 years is not yet known, and that late adverse effects may be reduced.

records.name: Mastectomy
records.tldr: Mastectomy removes breast tissue. The exact operation, nodal procedure and reconstruction are separate parts of the plan, and removal does not automatically eliminate the need for radiation or medicines.
records.summary:
Different mastectomy procedures remove different skin, nipple or chest-wall structures and may be accompanied by a separate nodal operation. The operative report specifies what was removed; pathology describes the examined tissue and boundaries. Neither the operation’s name nor a negative local finding establishes the absence of cancer throughout the body.

Reconstruction can use implants or a person’s tissue and may occur immediately or later. It addresses restoration or reshaping, rather than replacing indicated cancer treatment. Radiation and systemic therapy decisions retain disease extent, prior treatment and the full plan; a margin finding does not universally choose completion mastectomy over another approach.

When a mastectomy is recommended rather than chosen. Macmillan says surgeons try to do an operation that means you can keep your breast, and that a mastectomy may be recommended when the lump is large compared to the rest of the breast, when there is cancer in different parts of the breast (multicentric), when there is widespread DCIS, when the cancer is on the skin or in the underlying muscle, when you have had radiotherapy to the chest before to treat another cancer, or when you have a family history and have tested positive for a gene mutation.

A mastectomy does not always avoid radiotherapy. NICE NG101 (1.13.10) says to offer adjuvant postmastectomy radiotherapy to people with node-positive (macrometastases) invasive breast cancer or involved resection margins, (1.13.11) to consider it for node-negative T3 or T4 disease, and (1.13.12) not to offer it to people at low risk of local recurrence, for example most people with lymph node-negative breast cancer.

NICE NG101 (1.5.1) says to offer breast reconstruction to people after they have had a mastectomy for breast cancer, and (1.5.2) to be aware that some people may prefer not to have it. Cancer Research UK says a surgeon may be able to improve the appearance of the chest with further surgery after a mastectomy, and that a prosthesis is an alternative to reconstruction.

records.name: Breast reconstruction
records.tldr: Rebuilding the shape of a breast after a mastectomy, either with an implant or with the woman's own tissue, at the same operation or years later. In England every woman having a mastectomy for breast cancer must be offered it, and must be offered both timings whether or not the local hospital provides them.
records.summary:
There are two families of technique. Implant-based reconstruction uses a silicone implant, either placed at the mastectomy (direct to implant) or after a tissue expander has stretched the skin, and either behind the pectoralis major (sub-pectoral) or in front of it (pre-pectoral). Autologous reconstruction moves the woman's own skin and fat, most often from the lower abdomen as a deep inferior epigastric perforator flap, which spares the rectus muscle, and less often from the back (latissimus dorsi) or elsewhere. Reconstruction is immediate, at the same operation as the mastectomy, or delayed.

The honest comparison comes from the Mastectomy Reconstruction Outcomes Consortium, which followed 2,343 women for two years with both complications and a validated patient-reported questionnaire. Autologous reconstruction gave better satisfaction with the breasts (7.94 points higher, 5.68 to 10.20, p<0.001), psychosocial wellbeing and sexual wellbeing at two years. It also roughly doubled the odds of a complication: 1.97 (1.41 to 2.76) for a deep inferior epigastric perforator flap against expander-implant reconstruction. Implants failed more often, 7.1 percent against 1.3 percent for those flaps.

British practice has been measured twice and neither reading is comfortable. In iBRA, 2,081 women having immediate implant-based reconstruction at 81 units had implant loss of 9 percent, infection needing treatment of 25 percent, return to theatre of 18 percent and readmission of 18 percent within three months, all above the National Quality Standards of under 5 percent for the first three and under 10 percent for infection. Pre-BRA followed the newer pre-pectoral technique in 343 women and found implant loss of 8.2 percent and a complication in 42.0 percent, with physical and sexual wellbeing significantly below baseline at three and eighteen months.

The mesh question is unresolved. Biological or synthetic mesh, including acellular dermal matrix, is used to support the implant, and in iBRA 65 percent of reconstructions used it, 54 percent biological and 12 percent synthetic, without randomised evidence that it helps. Best-BRA, a pilot randomised trial of pre-pectoral against sub-pectoral placement, is the attempt to put that right.

On timing, NICE NG101 recommendation 1.5.1 offers reconstruction to everyone after a mastectomy for breast cancer, 1.5.3 offers both immediate and delayed options whether or not they are available locally, and 1.5.4 offers immediate reconstruction even to women who may need radiotherapy, unless another illness rules out the surgery. The guideline's own table warns that immediate reconstruction using implants may be affected by radiotherapy more than immediate flap reconstruction, and recommendation 1.13.14 allows the three-week radiotherapy schedule rather than the one-week one for women who have had implant-based reconstruction.

Breast implant-associated anaplastic large cell lymphoma is a rare cancer of the capsule around an implant and is covered separately.

records.name: Resection margins (R0 / R1 / R2)
records.tldr: Resection margins describe the assessed boundaries of removed tissue. A clear local boundary is not proof that no cancer exists elsewhere, and interpretation depends on the organ and reporting standard.
records.summary:
Margin assessment examines the cut boundaries of a submitted specimen and any additional margins. The operative account, sampled pathology and final residual-disease classification are connected but different observations. In the traditional R classification, R0 means no residual tumour under the applied assessment, R1 microscopic residual tumour and R2 gross residual tumour. These categories do not establish absence of every unseen cancer cell.

Definitions and required margin distances can vary by organ, disease and jurisdiction. The 2024 IASLC proposal describes an additional lung-cancer category for uncertain residual status. A clear microscopic edge is therefore not interchangeable with every definition of complete resection. Use the relevant report and standard rather than transferring a breast or pancreatic convention to every cancer.

notes: After breast conservation, further excision, completion mastectomy and axillary surgery address different findings and tissues. A second operation after initial pathology is not itself evidence of recurrence. Negative examined margins do not guarantee complete absence of microscopic disease.

For breast resection, final margin status uses the oriented main specimen together with relevant separately submitted margins. Ink identifies cut surfaces. An old main-specimen edge may cease to be the final edge when an additional oriented strip is removed; if their relationship is unclear, preserve uncertainty and request surgical correlation.

Report invasive carcinoma and DCIS separately, including the named final edge, whether the component reaches ink and its distance in millimetres when measurable. At ink is involved; a small gap without cancer at ink is a narrow negative margin. Ink artefact, limited sampling, compression and unclear orientation can limit interpretation.

The 2014 invasive-cancer consensus supported no ink on tumour for stage I to II invasive disease treated with breast conservation and whole-breast irradiation. Its evidence base excluded neoadjuvant therapy and pure DCIS. The 2016 pure-DCIS consensus supported a 2-mm adequate-margin standard with whole-breast irradiation; a narrower negative margin alone was not an indication for mastectomy. These are scoped standards, not interchangeable rules for every organ or operation.

In a fictional confirmed final edge with DCIS 0.7 mm from ink and no cancer at ink, the margin is narrow and negative rather than involved. Distance alone does not choose another operation. Conversely, invasive cancer at the confirmed outer edge of an additional lateral specimen remains a local margin finding even if a blood assay is negative.

Negative invasive margins and involved DCIS margins can coexist. A pCR definition permitting DCIS can coexist with a DCIS margin problem. The lymph-node capsule, a vessel lumen and a surgical cut edge are different boundaries. Margin status does not diagnose distant metastasis or whole-body clearance; completion excision, mastectomy and axillary surgery address different tissues.

A margin is a cut boundary of removed tissue. Pathology assesses sampled sections of that local boundary: a positive final margin means cancer reaches the evaluated cut edge. Sampling, sectioning and staining consume finite tissue, and cannot examine every possible cell. No ink on tumour does not mean no cancer anywhere in the person.

Pancreatic cancer uses a 1 mm rule: tumour within 1 mm of a margin is R1 (Royal College of Pathologists), which makes 76 to 85 percent of standardised head resections R1; the pancreatic glossary term carries the series and the ESPAC-3 survival by margin (Ghaneh 2019).

records.name: Margins after breast-conserving surgery, and second operations
records.tldr: After breast-conserving surgery, pathology assesses the removed tissue’s boundaries. The applicable standard, final specimen findings and treatment context guide whether further local treatment is considered.
records.summary: NICE NG101 says to offer further surgery, re-excision or mastectomy as appropriate, where invasive cancer or DCIS is present at the radial margins (tumour on ink, 0 mm); to consider further surgery after conserving surgery for invasive cancer with or without DCIS if tumour cells are present within 1 mm of but not at the radial margins; and to use 2 mm rather than 1 mm as the threshold for DCIS alone. The 2024 committee explained its reasoning plainly: a 1 mm margin is likely to achieve better breast preservation and result in fewer additional surgeries, repeated surgeries negatively affect breast appearance and can have a negative effect on self-esteem, and they are traumatic and can lead to stress, infection, pain and complications. It also noted that rates of further surgery currently vary across the country, and asked units to audit radial margins alongside recurrence. This is orientation from public patient pages, guidelines and the trials themselves, not advice for your case: your own team's instructions and 24-hour number come first, and no figure on this page is a prediction about you.

records.name: Lymph node status (node-positive / node-negative)
records.tldr: Lymph-node status classifies nodal involvement at a specified time and by a particular assessment. It does not measure every cancer cell throughout the body.
records.summary:
Clinical assessment before treatment and pathological assessment of removed nodes are different observations. Record the organ, method, timing, prefixes and modifiers rather than using positive or negative alone. A negative sampled-node result does not establish that every unsampled node is negative.

In the breast B-51 trial, clinical N1 described movable ipsilateral level I/II axillary involvement. Do not replace this clinical definition with a pathological one-to-three-node count. After neoadjuvant treatment, ypN0 is a pathological classification and can have modifiers. B-51 permitted ypN0i+ isolated tumour cells but did not collect their prevalence or specific outcomes.

The separate A011202 registry requires a nodal metastasis greater than 0.2 millimetres and treats deposits at or below 0.2 millimetres as N0i+. Those protocol rules do not make every use of positive or negative interchangeable. Nodal response alone is not a complete response in the breast or proof of whole-body clearance.

notes: For AJCC eighth-edition breast N categories, first preserve clinical cN, pathological pN or post-neoadjuvant ypN and the side and regional basin. Clinical cN1 describes movable ipsilateral level I/II axillary involvement, not a one-to-three-node surgical count. cN2a denotes fixed or matted level I/II nodes; cN2b internal mammary involvement without axillary involvement. cN3a, cN3b and cN3c describe infraclavicular, combined internal mammary/axillary and supraclavicular patterns respectively.

Pathological deposits use dimensions and cell context: isolated tumour cells are at most 0.2 mm, micrometastases exceed 0.2 mm but are at most 2 mm, and macrometastases exceed 2 mm. The approximately 200-cell guideline concerns one node profile, not counts added across levels. Dispersed minimal disease needs pathological judgement. ITC-only nodes are not counted as positive for AJCC N classification.

pN0(i+) denotes ITCs only; pN0(mol+) denotes molecular detection without histologically identified ITCs. pN1mi is micrometastatic disease only. If a macrometastasis is present, pN1a covers 1 to 3 involved axillary nodes, pN2a 4 to 9 and pN3a at least 10. Infraclavicular involvement is another location-defined route to pN3a. Nodes with micrometastases join the involved count when a macrometastasis exists; multiple micrometastases alone do not become pN2a.

Internal mammary sentinel involvement excluding ITCs is pN1b; combined with pN1a it is pN1c. Clinically detected internal mammary disease with pathologically negative axillary nodes is pN2b. pN3b includes pN1a or pN2a with clinically detected internal mammary involvement, or pN2a with internal mammary sentinel involvement; pN3c is ipsilateral supraclavicular involvement. These patterns cannot be reduced to node count alone.

A needle biopsy can confirm clinical involvement without measuring the entire deposit. Rare cN1mi requires the appropriate resected-node clinical context, rather than assigning a deposit size from needle material. If pathological nodes are unavailable, do not assume pN0. Intramammary nodes count with axillary nodes; regional ENE does not alone make N3 or M1.

Two of five involved means two among the five examined, not 40% of all regional nodes. Three 0.8-mm axillary deposits in a surgery-first example are pN1mi, whereas three involved axillary nodes including a 4-mm deposit support pN1a, assuming no other regional involvement. After therapy exclude adjacent treatment fibrosis from the contiguous residual staging dimension and retain baseline cN separately.

Clinical cN0 means no regional nodal metastasis identified by clinical assessment; cNX means regional nodes cannot be assessed. Level III axillary nodes are infraclavicular. Clinical cN3a is a location-based infraclavicular pattern; cN3b combines internal mammary and axillary involvement, and cN3c is supraclavicular. Ten involved axillary nodes is a pathological pN3a count criterion, not the definition of clinical cN3.

records.name: Completion surgery
records.tldr: Completion surgery is a further operation after an earlier procedure and its findings. The tissue, reason and clinical setting determine the question; a pathology finding does not select one operation automatically.
records.summary:
In breast care, further surgery can mean re-excision of a cavity, completion mastectomy or completion axillary dissection. These remove different tissues and address different findings. The final margin or node assessment, earlier treatment and full clinical context matter. A further operation after initial pathology is not itself a recurrence or a treatment for disease throughout the body.

Z0011 studied a specified surgery-first population receiving lumpectomy and planned whole-breast radiation. AMAROS compared axillary dissection with radiation, rather than with no axillary treatment. Those studies do not directly answer residual positive sentinel nodes after neoadjuvant chemotherapy; A011202 studies that different setting. Finding more involved nodes by removing them is different from preventing recurrence, and harms such as lymphoedema need separate assessment.

records.tldr: Regional nodal irradiation treats selected lymph-node regions. The exact fields, pretreatment findings and response after earlier therapy determine the clinical question.
records.summary:
Fields can include axillary, supraclavicular and internal mammary node regions, depending on the plan. This is distinct from breast or chest-wall irradiation, though they can be combined. After neoadjuvant treatment, ypN0 is a pathological nodal classification. Retain the sampled nodes and modifiers, including isolated-cell categories, rather than interpreting it as proof of absolute cellular absence or complete response in the breast.

B-51 studied biopsy-proven cT1 to T3 N1 M0 disease that became ypN0. Its primary recurrence-interval comparison was not statistically significant at median follow-up 59.5 months; this is not proof of zero effect in all settings. After lumpectomy both groups received whole-breast radiation. After mastectomy the contrast included chest-wall plus nodal radiation versus none.

A011202 instead studies residual positive sentinel nodes after neoadjuvant chemotherapy. Its registry describes dissection plus nodal radiation versus axillary and nodal radiation without dissection; both strategies include radiation. Do not transfer an omission conclusion between these different populations and contrasts. Organ exposure, lymphoedema and other harms remain part of the assessment.

records.name: T-cell exhaustion and CAR-T persistence
records.tldr: T-cell exhaustion describes altered differentiation and function under persistent stimulation. A marker, cell count or persisting CAR transgene does not by itself establish useful tumour killing.
records.summary:
Persistent stimulation can produce heterogeneous T-cell states, rather than one uniformly inactive population. In the studied tumour models, TCF1-positive, PD-1-positive cells could proliferate and generate more differentiated cells during checkpoint treatment. That result does not mean every exhausted cell has been reset. State-associated markers, receptor identity, proliferation and completed target-cell killing answer different questions.

For CAR-T, distinguish the infused preparation, expansion, later detection in blood, viable functional cells at relevant sites and disease control. A 24-patient axi-cel infusion-product study associated memory/exhaustion-related transcriptional features with outcomes; an association in that cohort does not prove that one modification will correct every failure. A detectable transgene is not itself a functional killing assay.

B-cell aplasia is used as a surrogate of CD19-directed activity against normal B cells, not a guarantee that all cancer sites remain controlled. Relapse can occur while aplasia continues. In the 2025 tisagenlecleucel analysis, relationships differed between B-ALL and diffuse large B-cell lymphoma; blood transgene levels lacked robust relapse-prediction performance. Early B-cell recovery in B-ALL was also affected by subsequent transplantation and censoring. No universal recovery cutoff or rule that persistence is irrelevant in ALL follows from an early response.

records.name: RECIST
records.tldr: RECIST 1.1 uses predefined anatomical measurements and other disease findings to classify response. A target sum is not every cancer site or total tumour volume.
records.summary:
RECIST 1.1 selects up to five measurable target lesions, with at most two per organ. Ordinary lesions contribute longest diameters; qualifying lymph nodes contribute short-axis measurements. Other disease is recorded separately, along with new lesions. The target sum is a selected measurement, rather than a complete inventory or volume of cancer.

For target lesions, partial response requires at least a 30 percent decrease from the baseline sum. Progression requires at least a 20 percent increase from the smallest sum on study, together with at least a five-millimetre absolute increase. Baseline is the progression reference if it remains the smallest sum. Unequivocal non-target progression or an unequivocal new malignant lesion can change the overall category despite shrinking targets.

Overall complete response requires the applicable target, non-target and new-lesion conditions, including short-axis reduction below ten millimetres for pathological nodes. Missing or equivocal findings require the protocol’s handling. Confirmation of response is not mandatory in every design: the guideline requires it for non-randomised trials whose primary endpoint is response.

Record the framework/version, selected lesions, dates, baseline, nadir, current values, acquisition comparability and findings outside the sum. iRECIST and metabolic PET criteria add different rules; an anatomical response does not establish tissue clearance, cure or a treatment decision.

records.name: iRECIST (response criteria for immunotherapy trials)
records.tldr: iRECIST provides trial-data rules for unconfirmed and confirmed progression during immunotherapy. An iUPD label does not prove pseudoprogression or automatically permit continued treatment.
records.summary:
The 2017 consensus adapted RECIST 1.1 for consistent data collection in immunotherapy trials. Progression first receives the iUPD, or immune unconfirmed progressive disease, label. Subsequent findings can confirm iCPD or meet another category under the framework; unchanged findings do not automatically erase iUPD. Target, non-target and new-lesion categories retain their own rules.

For trials permitting treatment beyond iUPD, the guideline limits continuation to clinically stable participants, with reassessment generally four to eight weeks later. Stability includes performance status, disease-related symptoms and the need for intensified symptom management. The working group also describes protocol and scheduling exceptions; the interval is not an independent instruction for personal care.

The framework records possible atypical response patterns without assuming that apparent worsening is pseudoprogression. It concerns trial data handling, while continuation or discontinuation decisions remain with the participant and clinical team. The primary guideline and later working-group clarifications do not make the category a universally validated treatment-selection rule.

records.name: PERCIST (PET response criteria in solid tumours)
aka: PET Response Criteria in Solid Tumors
records.tldr: PERCIST 1.0 is a proposed FDG-PET response framework using lean-body-mass-normalised uptake. Its response rule needs more than a percentage change alone.
records.summary:
The 2009 PERCIST 1.0 proposal measures FDG activity using SUL, an uptake value normalised to lean body mass. It uses a small peak-uptake region of about one cubic centimetre, with reference tissue and suitability requirements. Consistent acquisition, calibration, preparation and timing matter; normalisation alone does not make two scans comparable.

In Table 7, partial metabolic response requires at least a 30 percent reduction in the target SUL peak and an absolute drop of at least 0.8 SUL units, together with the other disease and technical conditions. New lesions or progression elsewhere cannot be ignored. The most active assessed lesion after treatment need not be the same lesion as before. A percentage-only cutoff therefore does not implement the proposal.

Metabolic and anatomical criteria measure different properties. The original proposal defers to RECIST 1.1 when FDG avidity or technical suitability is inadequate, and describes continuing validation needs. A metabolic response does not establish pathological complete response, disappearance of every tumour cell or individual treatment benefit.

Selected PERCIST 1.0 baseline conditions: measure SUL peak in an approximately one-cubic-centimetre sphere, about 1.2 cm across. The proposed measurable-lesion threshold is at least 1.5 times normal-liver mean SUL plus two standard deviations, using a 3-cm spherical liver reference. An abnormal liver requires the alternative blood-pool reference and its own rules. Table 7 also requires comparable reference uptake, tracer timing, calibration and acquisition; a threshold or lean-mass correction alone is insufficient.

The 2009 proposal advises waiting at least 10 days after chemotherapy to reduce transient effects on FDG uptake, while recognising that optimal timing is treatment-specific and other disease guidance can use longer intervals. This is a condition of that cited framework, not a personal scan-scheduling instruction or a universal interval after every treatment.

Table 7 defines complete metabolic response by target uptake below liver mean and indistinguishable from background blood pool, disappearance of other lesions to background, and no new cancer-typical FDG-avid lesions. An anatomical progression finding requires verification. Complete metabolic response does not require a zero uptake value. Stable metabolic disease meets none of the complete, partial or progressive metabolic definitions.

For the SUL-peak route to progressive metabolic disease, Table 7 specifies a rise greater than 30 percent and greater than 0.8 SUL units from baseline, in a pattern typical of tumour rather than infection or treatment effect. It also describes increased-extent/total-lesion-glycolysis and new cancer-typical-lesion routes. Its confirmation rules and visceral-lesion or clear RECIST-progression exceptions matter. For partial metabolic response, the percentage and absolute decline already stated must also satisfy the original other-lesion, new-lesion and anatomical-verification conditions. Use the complete framework and protocol rather than a percentage-only shortcut.

A 2017 analysis by Riedl and colleagues included 65 people with metastatic breast cancer receiving first- or second-line systemic therapy in prospective trials. All 22 RECIST responders also responded by PERCIST; 17 of 43 RECIST non-responders responded by PERCIST. The PFS concordance index was 0.70 for PERCIST versus 0.60 for RECIST. Four-year disease-specific survival was 58 percent in PERCIST responders and 18 percent in non-responders. These are cohort-level prognostic associations in response-defined groups. They do not establish benefit from changing treatment according to PERCIST, and are not a TNBC-specific or individual prognosis.

records.name: Quantitative imaging biomarkers (RECIST, PERCIST, SUV, ADC)
records.tldr: Quantitative imaging extracts measurements such as lesion dimensions or tracer uptake from scans. Their accuracy, interpretation and clinical usefulness require different evidence.
records.summary:
Quantitative imaging produces numerical estimates from images or imaging data. Lesion dimensions, FDG uptake and MRI-derived measures describe specified properties, rather than directly counting living or dead cancer cells. Response criteria interpret particular measurements alongside other disease findings; organ-specific risk categories have different purposes. Neither is a universal endpoint for every oncology trial.

The 2022 FDA technical-performance guidance separates the quantity being estimated from the value an algorithm reports. Systematic error, random variation, patient preparation and physiology, acquisition hardware/protocol, reconstruction, segmentation and software can affect a result. Assess specifications and supporting data for the stated intended use, population and operating range; no single precision claim applies to every measurement.

QIBA documents describe technical performance claims and the conditions or stages attached to profiles. A profile title does not establish that a particular site or tool conforms, and technical performance alone does not validate a treatment-benefit prediction. Clinical interpretation and utility need their own evidence. A response or progression category is not an automatic command to stop or continue treatment, as the iRECIST framework explicitly illustrates.

records.tldr: This randomised phase 2 trial found longer progression-free survival with a specified subtype-based combination strategy than with nab-paclitaxel alone, with more serious treatment-related adverse events.

At the 31 May 2023 cutoff, median follow-up was 22.5 months (interquartile range 15.2-29.0). It tested a package of classification, matching rules and regimens; it did not separately establish each component's effect.

At the 31 May 2023 cutoff, median follow-up was 22.5 months (interquartile range 15.2-29.0). It tested a package of classification, matching rules and regimens; it did not separately establish each component's effect.

records.name: Synthetic cytokine receptors
records.tldr: An engineered cytokine receptor connects a specified input to signalling inside a cell. The added signal and the behaviour of the complete cell product need separate measurements.
records.summary: A synthetic cytokine receptor is an engineered cell-surface protein that connects a specified input to intracellular signalling. It differs from engineering a soluble cytokine or simply administering a cytokine. Some designs require an externally supplied ligand; others generate ligand-independent signalling. The receptor domains, input, expression and cell type define the tested construct. A growth-supporting signal does not itself establish antigen recognition, entry into a tumour, completed killing or durable patient benefit.

notes: Engelowski and colleagues joined fluorescent-protein-binding nanobodies to selected cytokine-receptor membrane and intracellular domains. Artificial GFP/mCherry-based ligands induced signalling in experimental systems. That 2018 study is a particular ligand-dependent design, not a test of every synthetic receptor or of a company platform with a different architecture.

In a 2010 human T-cell study, a chimeric receptor joined the IL-4 receptor binding region to an IL-2/IL-15 receptor signalling component. IL-4 supported expansion of the engineered cells, while a separate CAR specified the tumour target. The reported culture experiments distinguished expansion, cytokine dependence and target-cell killing; they were not patient efficacy results.

A 2026 macrophage preprint studied ligand-independent receptors with varied signalling motifs in primary human macrophages and preclinical models. Marker expression, phagocytosis and mouse tumour observations were different readouts. The report remains a preprint and does not establish human treatment benefit.

Enoda uses MIMIC as the name of its synthetic cytokine-receptor assets. The platform name does not define all engineered cytokine receptors or establish clinical performance. Its website describes platform aims and sponsor claims; it is not a comparative clinical safety or efficacy report.

For a drug-gated construct, withdrawing the input can reduce a selected signal without eliminating cells already engineered. Receptor signalling, viable-cell counts, tissue location, target-cell killing and later disease control need distinct measurements. A growth or activity switch is different from a cell-elimination mechanism.
A mechanistic schematic shows an intended arrangement. It is not a measurement of receptor expression, signalling, cell killing or patient outcome; each of those requires its own evidence.

records.name: Allogeneic (off-the-shelf) cell therapy
records.tldr: Allogeneic cell therapy uses cells from someone other than the recipient. A banked product may avoid collecting the recipient's cells, but treatment still requires a suitable product and clinical preparation.
records.summary: Autologous cells come from the intended recipient; allogeneic cells come from another person. This source distinction is separate from whether engineering occurs outside or inside the body and from whether a cell product or a carrier is administered. Donor-cell manufacture can provide inventory for later recipients, but usable supply, quality disposition, matching requirements, preparation and clinical eligibility still govern access. Donor immune cells can attack recipient tissues, while the recipient's immune system can reject donor cells. The relevant mechanisms depend on cell type, construct, edits, conditioning and setting.

FDA: CAR T-cell development guidance, January 2024
Qasim et al., 2017: two-infant donor CAR T-cell report
Benjamin et al., 2020: early UCART19 child and adult cohorts
Dupouy et al., 2022: adult CALM cellular kinetics and manufacturing context
Chen et al., 2024: distinct edits, laboratory models and nine recipients
ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT03229876, dated registry state differs from publication wording

notes: Disrupting TRAC can reduce endogenous alpha-beta T-cell receptor activity in a specified T-cell product. HLA changes address different recognition pathways. Broad loss of class I HLA can also expose cells to natural-killer-cell rejection. CD52 disruption has a distinct role in allowing an engineered product to resist an anti-CD52 conditioning antibody. These modifications are not interchangeable and are not required in every allogeneic cell type.

Qasim's 2017 report described two infants given donor CAR T cells edited at TRAC and CD52, with lymphodepletion including an anti-CD52 antibody and subsequent allogeneic transplantation. Benjamin's 2020 report combined early cohorts of seven children and fourteen adults; graft-versus-host disease, cytokine release syndrome, infections and treatment-related deaths were reported. A source or edit label does not eliminate clinical risks. These are small, uncontrolled reports, and their participant counts must not be added to later overlapping CALM analyses.

Dupouy's 2022 analysis concerns twenty-five adults in CALM, not a separate additional cohort to sum with earlier CALM recipients. Nine batches from six donors were infused. Blood transgene kinetics, flow cytometry, donor/product characteristics and conditioning exposure were examined separately. Associations between alemtuzumab exposure and expansion do not establish a randomised conditioning comparison or a universal need for deeper lymphodepletion.

Chen's 2024 report includes cell and mouse experiments plus nine treated people. Six recipients received B2M/TRAC-disrupted cells without observed in-body expansion or antitumour response; three received HLA-A/HLA-B/TRAC-disrupted cells and had early MRD-negative responses. These groups were small and differently prepared, not a randomised test of editing alone. No observed graft-versus-host disease in nine recipients is not proof of zero risk or durable benefit.

Chen's paper calls the study phase 1, whereas the captured NCT03229876 registry record has phase NA and overall status suspended, with a last posted update of 24 July 2023. This source/version discrepancy is retained; the paper is not evidence that treatment is currently available.

Persistence is a measured outcome, not a fixed property of donor origin. Blood detection differs from distribution across tissues and useful cell function; conditioning before a later transplant can end observation of a product. Availability also requires the intended source, construct version, lot, dose and recipient relationships to remain traceable.
records.principle: Keep cell source, engineering location, administered material and each direction of immune recognition distinct; evaluate the actual construct and clinical cohort.
strengths: Can manufacture and bank donor-derived cells ahead of an individual recipient's treatment
Investigates supply from a source other than the recipient's own collection
limitations: Gene editing does not guarantee absence of graft-versus-host disease or rejection
Conditioning, infections, toxicity and persistence require product-specific evidence
Banked inventory does not establish immediate availability, eligibility or clinical benefit

records.name: Apheresis (leukapheresis)
records.tldr: Apheresis separates components from blood and returns other components to the circulation. Leukapheresis collects a white-cell-rich mixture that can be starting material for a cell therapy or research.
records.summary: Leukapheresis uses an extracorporeal separation circuit to collect white-cell-rich material. A leukopak can contain lymphocytes and monocytes in variable proportions; it is not automatically a purified T-cell population or a released treatment. The collection method, intended cells and receiving programme determine the required material, measurements and handling. Collection for a cell therapy, research or a stem-cell procedure retains its own protocol rather than sharing one duration or universal preparation rule.

FDA: CAR T-cell development guidance, January 2024
NIH consent library version 18: supervised leukapheresis, February 2026

notes: Processed blood volume, collected bag volume, total white-cell number, viable-cell recovery and numbers or fractions of intended subsets are different measurements. A large bag or high overall white-cell count does not establish an adequate viable T-cell input. FDA's CAR T-cell guidance recommends product-development-specific starting-material acceptance criteria and discusses CD3, CD4, CD8, NK-cell, monocyte and B-cell characterisation.

Collection is supervised clinical care. Access may use peripheral veins or a central catheter. Citrate anticoagulant can lower available calcium and cause symptoms requiring monitoring or treatment; access, blood-pressure, bleeding and infection risks depend on the procedure and person. The NIH consent example is not a universal duration, risk estimate or permission to change medicines.

Prior treatment, current cell composition, collection and shipping conditions can affect the starting material. Retain source identity, time, handling, receiving acceptance and relevant samples through subsequent manufacture. A successful collection does not guarantee culture growth, a conforming final lot or eventual infusion.

Research collection and therapeutic collection can have different acceptance, consent, banking and testing requirements. Tumour-infiltrating-lymphocyte manufacture uses tumour-derived material, not simply this blood collection. Vaccines and other cell-based protocols have their own collection requirements; leukapheresis is not a universal prerequisite for vaccination.

records.name: Cryopreservation and cell-therapy cold chain
records.tldr: Freezing, storage, shipping and thawing can preserve cells for later use. The validated conditions and checks belong to the particular cell product.
records.summary: Cryopreservation manages cooling, water movement, ice formation, concentrated solutes and warming injury; it does not literally stop all molecular motion. Cryoprotectant formulation, exposure, freezing, storage, transport, thawing and permitted holding times form a defined process. Some materials are handled fresh. A temperature log documents conditions, while stability evidence and the quality system determine the consequences of a deviation. Neither a shipper nor a barcode guarantees viable, functional material or the correct recipient.

DailyMed: KYMRIAH label captured 9 November 2026, sections 11 and 16
Mazur, 1963: water movement and intracellular freezing
Panch et al., 2019: scoped fresh/frozen CAR T-cell comparisons
Wang et al., 2019: post-thaw assay conditions for one CAR T-cell preparation

notes: The labels captured on 9 November 2026 illustrate why a single temperature or formulation is misleading. YESCARTA describes 5% DMSO with 2.5% human albumin, whereas KYMRIAH describes 7.5% (v/v) DMSO. These are particular labelled formulations, not a general recipe for other cells, research specimens, RNA or carrier products.

The captured YESCARTA section 16 distinguishes shipment at minus 150 degrees Celsius or colder from storage at minus 120 degrees or colder, and describes bounded transfers and a one-time minus 80 degrees plus or minus 10 degrees storage option for up to 90 days without exceeding expiry. Its transfer restrictions matter. KYMRIAH section 16 specifies monitored storage at minus 120 degrees or colder and its own transport provisions. Consult the complete current label and product procedures; these examples do not authorise an unlisted excursion or an improvised thaw/rest schedule.

In a fictional input of 100 million viable cells, 80 million cells are recovered after processing and 72 million of those are live. Recovered-cell viability is 72/80, or 90%, while viable recovery relative to input is 72/100, or 72%. The missing 20 million are not silently included among tested recovered cells. Neither fraction measures the intended biological activity or establishes a release threshold.

Panch's 2019 retrospective single-centre analysis covered 158 autologous CAR T-cell products from six trials and additional donor experiments. It did not detect differences in selected manufacturing or clinical measures under its tested conditions, while molecular and cellular changes were observed. This does not demonstrate universal equivalence of fresh and frozen material or interchangeability of starting-material and final-product freezing.

Wang's 2019 work concerns an in vitro post-thaw potency assay for a particular third-generation CD19 CAR T-cell preparation. Assay recovery or rest conditions are not instructions to change clinical preparation or infusion. Preserve sampling time, denominator, cell composition and intended test when comparing results.

Research banking and clinical cell-product storage have different intended uses and acceptance requirements. An excursion requires documented investigation, relevant stability evidence and a disposition by the authorised programme. Identity records, custody records, temperature logs, test samples and final-product decisions remain distinct.
records.principle: Validate preservation and transport for the specified material and intended use; distinguish documented handling, recovered-cell viability, input-relative recovery and biological activity.
strengths: Can separate collection, manufacture and administration in a validated workflow
Supports banking and transport when the particular material remains suitable under demonstrated conditions
limitations: Freezing, warming and cryoprotectant exposure can change cell recovery, state or function
Conditions and permitted excursions cannot be transferred between products without evidence
Traceability and temperature records do not replace quality assessment or authorised disposition

records.name: Cell-therapy orchestration and chain-of-identity software
records.tldr: Scheduling and tracking software can support a cell therapy's collection, manufacture, transport and treatment records. It helps teams follow the workflow and investigate problems.
records.summary: Orchestration systems can coordinate appointments, inventory, material identifiers, handoffs, manufacturing status and clinical scheduling. Their records must preserve the actual source, material, construct, lot, sample, dose and intended-recipient relationships. Software supports a controlled workflow; it does not by itself eliminate mix-ups, deliver on-time treatment or establish product quality. FDA's traceability requirements and recommendations do not require the named commercial platforms previously listed here.

notes: Chain of identity concerns the association between source, materials, product and intended recipient. Chain of custody concerns guardianship, handoffs, times and relevant handling conditions. A temperature trace is handling evidence; an HLA result is a biological measurement. Neither substitutes for the complete recipient/material relationship or the quality decision.

A collection can branch into separate processing lots, doses and test samples. Retain parent links and the construct version when a process changes. A single-recipient branching example does not define every donor-bank or multi-recipient workflow; validate the actual product relationships.

FDA's January 2024 CAR T-cell guidance describes documented labelling and tracking from collection through administration, unique-identifier recommendations for autologous products, and independent bedside patient/label checks. Compliance is assessed against applicable requirements and a controlled process, not the presence of a particular vendor's portal.

A completed software workflow is not a potency result, a stability conclusion, an authorised lot disposition or a patient eligibility decision. Discrepancies need reconciliation and investigation; a reported excursion does not determine its own clinical significance.
records.principle: Maintain controlled, reconcilable records across the actual workflow, with identifiers and recorded handoffs supporting separate identity and quality decisions.
strengths: Can make status, handoffs and scheduling information available to responsible teams
Can support reconciliation, traceability and investigation when records and interfaces are controlled
limitations: Incorrect inputs or broken links can propagate across connected systems
A recorded handoff or barcode does not establish identity, acceptable quality or clinical readiness
Workflow design, access controls, integration and contingency arrangements need evaluation

records.name: Autologous CAR-T manufacturing, batch by batch
records.tldr: An autologous CAR T-cell product is made from the intended recipient's cells. Collection, engineering, culture, quality assessment and treatment scheduling are distinct steps.
records.summary: A defined ex vivo process receives starting material, selects or enriches cells as needed, activates and engineers them, cultures them under controlled conditions, and prepares material for testing, storage and administration. The sequence, vector or other gene-transfer method, culture duration, fresh or frozen handling and assays depend on the product. A collection, manufacturing run, product lot, test sample and administered dose are not interchangeable units. One collection can yield multiple containers or doses; a run need not culminate in an infused treatment.

21 CFR Part 1271: human cells, tissues and cellular products
Wikipedia
FDA: CAR T-cell development guidance, January 2024
FDA: human gene-therapy IND CMC guidance, January 2020

notes: Enrichment changes the composition of a mixture; activation changes cell state; expansion increases the absolute number of a defined living population. Measure the intended population consistently before and after culture. A higher percentage, a different volume or a higher concentration alone does not demonstrate expansion.

Release evidence retains identity, purity, viable amount, intended biological activity and relevant contamination risks. Some tests can continue after disposition only within a justified and authorised setting with appropriate follow-up. Neither receptor expression nor a viable-cell count alone establishes every required function.

Culture duration is only one clock. Collection-to-infusion also includes material acceptance, transport, processing, testing, clinical reassessment and scheduling, with steps sometimes overlapping. A number measured among infused recipients does not describe people who never reached infusion. Avoid a universal week range or a cross-product timing ranking.

Manufacturing can end without a product, yield a product outside specified requirements, or provide a conforming lot that is never administered. A lack of a collection or treatment slot is another access event. Keep the report's event definition, denominator, period and cancellation rules with any rate.

The process remains traceable through collections, intermediate material, product lots, doses and samples. Source and intended-recipient matching, biological identity testing, custody and conditions, lot disposition and clinical readiness each require their own evidence.

FDA's 2024 document focuses on ex vivo CAR T-cell development. Its recommendations do not automatically validate every in vivo carrier, other immune-cell product or research-bank process. Process changes need relevant evidence rather than a promise that automation or shorter culture preserves all attributes.

In a separate fictional cohort, ten people undergo collection and eight receive an infusion. The two never infused are reported separately; they are not assigned the collection-to-infusion time calculated among the eight. State the follow-up window and reasons for non-infusion before interpreting this proportion.
records.principle: Retain the product-specific process, starting material, defined cell population, parent/lot/dose relationships, control strategy and separate manufacturing and clinical outcomes.
strengths: Supports a defined recipient-linked manufacturing and quality-control process
Individual steps can be studied and improved with relevant comparability and functional evidence
limitations: Starting-material variability, contamination, growth or engineering problems can prevent a suitable product
A completed lot, a conforming lot, shipment and infusion are distinct outcomes
Shorter culture does not establish a shorter total wait, equivalent quality or better clinical outcomes

records.name: Cell-product chain of identity and custody
records.tldr: Identity records connect cells and products to their source and intended recipient. Custody records show who held them and what happened during handoffs.
records.summary: Traceability preserves relationships across source material, engineering construct, processing lots, containers, samples and intended recipients. Chain of identity and chain of custody answer different questions: what material and recipient are associated, and who had responsibility at each stage under which recorded conditions. A coded identifier makes a relationship recordable; it does not independently prove that the label, material and recipient agree.

ICCBBA: Chain of Identity standard ST-028, version 1.1.0 (June 2025)
ICCBBA: single-patient collection examples IG-050, version 1.0.0 (December 2023)

notes: A collection can branch into processing lots, doses or test samples. Retain parent links and construct versions so a sample result can be attributed to the material it represents. One bag need not mean one manufacturing run or one dose; an allogeneic workflow can relate donor material to later recipients according to its actual design.

ICCBBA ST-028 version 1.1.0, June 2025, describes chain-of-identity relationships and responsibilities. IG-050 version 1.0.0, December 2023, gives bounded examples in which material is returned to the same patient; it explicitly does not cover one collection manufactured into therapies for multiple patients. That example scope must not be generalised into a complete donor-bank scheme.

In a fictional single-recipient example, collection A produces lot A, which branches into doses A1 and A2 and test sample S. Each child retains the parent link. A separate custody trail records handlers, handoff times and conditions. Keeping those links does not establish acceptable quality or clinical suitability.

Barcodes, biological identity assays, HLA typing, potency results and temperature traces are different evidence. None alone replaces the complete material/intended-recipient verification. A discrepancy or excursion requires investigation and the authorised quality disposition; an audit trail is evidence to assess, not a guarantee of safety.

FDA's CAR T-cell guidance addresses documented tracking from collection to administration and independent recipient/label checks. The required process is not equivalent to purchasing a particular orchestration system. Research samples, fresh products, cryopreserved products and in vivo carriers retain their own applicable identities and handling context.

records.name: Ex vivo cell expansion
records.tldr: Cell expansion increases the number of a defined group of living cells outside the body. Selecting cells or activating them answers a different question.
records.summary: Expansion compares absolute counts of a specified living population at stated points in a culture process. Enrichment or selection changes mixture composition, while activation changes cellular state. Measurements need a consistent cell definition, viability basis, sampling method and interval. Cell concentration can change with dilution or volume, and a higher fraction can result from losing other cells rather than producing more intended cells.

links.label: FDA: CAR T-cell development guidance, January 2024
Ghassemi et al., 2018: defined culture-duration comparisons and mouse experiments
Dupouy et al., 2022: factory expansion and adult CALM cellular kinetics

notes: In a fictional mixture, 20 million intended cells and 80 million other cells become 20 million intended and five million other cells after enrichment. The intended fraction rises from 20/100 to 20/25 without increasing the intended-cell count. In a separate culture example, 20 million viable intended cells becoming 100 million is five-fold expansion. These are invented arithmetic examples, not process-performance targets.

Culture conditions, activation, gene transfer, duration, selection and preservation can change subsets, differentiation, viability and function. A greater count does not establish equal starting-cell quality, a favourable state or greater tumour killing. Activation markers and intended biological activity require suitable separate measurements.

Ghassemi's 2018 study compared shorter and longer preparation in human CAR T-cell experiments, a mouse acute-lymphoblastic-leukaemia model and manufacturing-feasibility work. The reported culture comparison does not prove that every shorter process improves human outcomes or specify one optimal duration for all products.

Dupouy's adult CALM analysis distinguishes factory fold expansion from later blood transgene and flow-cytometry kinetics. In-body detection depends on sampling, proliferation, distribution, loss and expression. A blood copy count is not an absolute whole-body count or a direct functional assay.

Expansion can be one input to a product-specific control strategy. It does not replace identity, purity, viability, potency, contamination testing, lot disposition or clinical readiness. Manufacturing yield, culture time, collection-to-infusion time and patient benefit remain separate outcomes.

records.name: Cell-manufacturing outcomes and nonconforming products
records.tldr: Making a cell product, meeting its quality requirements, shipping it and treating a person are different outcomes. A report's definition and denominator determine what its success rate means.
records.summary: A process can stop without a product, produce a nonconforming lot, make a conforming product that is never shipped, or supply material that is never infused. Out-of-specification means at least one stated requirement was missed; it does not determine which attribute, severity or disposition applies. Studies sometimes include such lots within manufacturing failure, while others report separate categories. Keep orders, collections, runs, batches, people, cancellations and follow-up with the reported measure.

Kato et al., 2025: single-arm nonconforming tisagenlecleucel cohort

notes: In a fictional 100-collection pathway, 94 produce completed products, four of those 94 miss a stated specification, and 85 people are ultimately infused. Completion, conformity and infusion have different numerators and can require different denominators. These invented numbers do not define a standard manufacturing-success metric, describe a real cohort or imply that an out-of-specification product was used.

Iwamoto's 2025 report covers Japanese tisagenlecleucel manufacturing from August 2019 to July 2023. Its manufacturing-success numerator is batches meeting health-authority release criteria; its shipment-success numerator also includes selected nonconforming products made available for shipment. Both use initiated batches excluding specified cancellations during manufacturing. Cancellation rate instead uses all initiated batches and can include cancellations after receipt. The methods report no formal statistical analysis; observed before/after changes do not isolate a causal process effect.

The UK National CAR T Panel's 2025 retrospective report uses manufacturing failure to include no product and out-of-specification product. Approved, remanufactured, infused and never-infused people remain separate groups. Its report of no statistically significant outcome differences is not a demonstration of equivalence, and its associations do not establish individual risk or treatment selection.

Kato's 2025 single-arm Japanese report enrolled 29 people and infused 28, with 23 DLBCL and five ALL recipients. Response was assessed in 15 of the 23 DLBCL recipients; it is not correct to give the evaluable response denominator as all 23. The abstract's batch denominators also differ by missed attribute: low viability 15/24, low dose 8/23 DLBCL and high dose 4/5 ALL. Do not combine those fractions or treat single-arm comparisons as proof of equal safety or efficacy.

The Kato report's NCT04094311 identifies a specific clinical supply pathway for nonconforming tisagenlecleucel. The captured registry remains a larger recruiting study with no posted results, not just that dated published cohort. Registry design, national supply rules and a report of use do not authorise use of another nonconforming lot or establish a local treatment slot.

Record the missed specification, test method, material, lot, jurisdiction and programme. Selected access can involve a separate authorised pathway and case-specific quality and clinical assessment; a low-viability miss is not interchangeable with a dose miss or contamination. A conforming product also does not establish patient readiness or clinical benefit.
